title: Single-molecule imaging of HIV-1 RNA translation reveals rapid kinetics and nucleocapsid-dependent efficiency.
abstract: The HIV-1 full-length RNA (FL-RNA) serves both as the viral genome and as the messenger RNA encoding the Gag and Gag-Pol polyproteins. Regulation of FL-RNA translation is therefore central to HIV-1 gene expression and replication. The nucleocapsid domain of Gag (NC) is a multifunctional RNA-binding protein best known for its role in genomic RNA packaging, yet its potential contribution to viral RNA translation remains poorly understood. Here, we used single-molecule imaging to visualize translation of HIV-1 FL-RNA in living cells. We engineered an HIV-1 molecular clone containing SunTag repeats in Gag and MS2 stem-loops in the viral RNA and analyzed mutants of the NC domain impaired in RNA binding. We found that only a subset of cytoplasmic FL-RNA molecules is actively translated under our experimental conditions, and that NC deletion reduced this fraction. Live-cell imaging revealed rapid elongation kinetics (~24 amino acids per second) and heterogeneous polysomes containing multiple ribosomes per viral RNA. Deletion of the NC zinc-fingers or of the entire NC domain markedly reduced twice the ribosome loading onto individual RNAs without affecting elongation speed but decreasing initiation time. Together, these results provide a quantitative view of HIV-1 FL-RNA translation dynamics in living cells and identify the nucleocapsid domain as a key determinant of efficient ribosome loading on the viral genome.

title: Sequence resources of the National Center for Biotechnology Information in 2027.
abstract: The National Center for Biotechnology Information (NCBI) provides three principal resources containing DNA, RNA, and protein sequence data: the Sequence Read Archive (SRA), GenBank®, and the Reference Sequence (RefSeq™) collection. All resources are free to the public. SRA and GenBank are part of the International Nucleotide Sequence Database Collaboration and share data daily. After summarizing the current state of these resources, we review significant updates in the past two years, including these to the Submission Portal, the primary interface for submitting data to SRA and GenBank. We also describe access points for these data including NCBI Datasets' website and programmatic interface, and present improvements in NCBI's main sequence analysis and visualization tools, such as annotation pipelines, BLAST, and the Multiple Comparative Genome Viewer.

title: Spatially Patterned Heteromultivalency Enhances Nucleic Acid Recognition at Nanochannel Outer Surface.
abstract: Solid-state nanochannels offer a versatile platform for label-free biosensing by transducing interfacial target recognition into ionic current signals. However, the sensing performance of such systems has mainly relied on regulating probe grafting density, while the impact of probe architecture and nanoscale spatial organization remains insufficiently explored. Here, we report a nanochannel biosensor constructed by immobilizing spatially patterned heteromultivalent probes at the outer surface of gold-coated polyethylene terephthalate nanochannels (PHP@OS) to enhance nucleic acid capture. We show that target binding at nanochannel outer surface induces changes in surface charge that enhance ionic current. Compared with homomultivalent and randomly arranged heteromultivalent designs, the spatially patterned interface exhibits up to approximately 6.6-fold higher hybridization efficiency and 7-fold faster binding kinetics, together with an approximately 3-10-fold improvement in apparent binding affinity. Moreover, the PHP@OS enables sensitive and selective detection of bacterial 16S ribosomal RNA in cell lysate samples, highlighting the robustness of this design under biologically relevant conditions. This work demonstrates that spatially organized heteromultivalent probe architectures provide an effective route to engineer the outer surface for high-performance nanochannel biosensing and may be extended to other biomolecular sensing systems by tailoring probe architecture and spatial organization.

title: Noncoding RNAs in Nuclear Condensates and RNA Processing in Skeletal Muscle.
abstract: Spatial organization in the nucleus is an active layer of RNA regulation in skeletal muscle, yet localization is often interpreted more strongly than the evidence permits. This critical review compares physiological nuclear RNA compartments with pathological repeat-RNA assemblies using a graded evidence framework. NEAT1-associated paraspeckles provide the clearest muscle-linked example of an RNA-marked nuclear body, although isoform-specific architectural causality remains untested in muscle. MALAT1 regulates speckle-associated splicing-factor and chromatin states but is dispensable for gross speckle formation, and muscle studies report opposing differentiation phenotypes. Nucleolar FRG2 transcripts in facioscapulohumeral muscular dystrophy connect spatial RNA organization to rDNA transcription and translational capacity. Expanded DMPK CUG and CNBP CCUG RNAs in myotonic dystrophy sequester processing factors and drive spliceopathy, although calibrated imaging in patient-derived DM1 myotubes indicates that most apparent foci are individual retained transcripts rather than bulk condensates. The framework distinguishes spatial association, molecular participation, functional necessity, in vivo relevance, and therapeutic target engagement. It also maps interventions to toxic-RNA abundance, RNA-protein binding, repeat-locus transcription, downstream splicing, or compartment state. Together, this evidence-based synthesis identifies which nuclear RNA mechanisms are established in muscle, which remain extrapolated from non-muscle systems, and which experiments are required before therapeutic modulation can be interpreted mechanistically.

title: Beyond the Neuron: TDP-43 and the Challenge of Pre-Analytical Quality in Platelet Biomarker Development.
abstract: TAR DNA-binding protein 43 (TDP-43) is the primary pathological hallmark of amyotrophic lateral sclerosis (ALS) and frontotemporal dementia (FTD). Yet, despite two decades of intensive research, a reliable peripheral TDP-43 biomarker remains elusive. Recognizing platelets as a major blood reservoir of TDP-43 opens new diagnostic avenues but may also reveal potential vulnerabilities. In this narrative review, we first trace the evolving understanding of TDP-43 from a nuclear RNA-binding protein to a molecule whose functions and disease-associated alterations extend beyond the neuron. We then examine recent breakthroughs demonstrating that TDP-43 function is shaped by its cellular environment and how it may be uniquely concentrated in platelets. Next, we argue that pre-analytical variables, such as hemolysis, clotting, cold-chain failures, and biobank protocols, are not mere "noise" but potential confounders that distort molecular integrity and should be taken into account. Finally, we discuss the biological and methodological uncertainties surrounding platelet TDP-43 and highlight how standardized handling and systematic pre-analytical reporting can improve reproducibility and support future biomarker validation. More broadly, the methodological standards outlined in this review may extend beyond TDP-43 to other disease-related proteins that are present in platelets and similarly sensitive to pre-analytical variability.

title: Integrated Plasma snoRNA-Protein Network Analysis Identifies Circulating Molecular Signatures Associated with High-Risk Benign Breast Lesions and Early Breast Cancer.
abstract: High-risk benign breast lesions increase subsequent breast cancer risk, yet circulating molecular patterns that distinguish them from early breast cancer remain poorly defined. We profiled plasma small nucleolar RNAs (snoRNAs) and small Cajal body-specific RNAs (scaRNAs) using UMI-based small RNA sequencing in 32 plasma samples from patients with low-risk benign lesions (Be; 9), high-risk benign lesions (HB; 14), or early breast cancer (CA; 9), and integrated matched data-independent acquisition (DIA) proteomics in a subset of 20 samples (HB; 11, CA; 9). Weighted gene co-expression network analysis (WGCNA) of 475 molecular features identified 11 modules. The Yellow module contained 25 snoRNAs/scaRNAs and 26 proteins and was enriched for extracellular matrix (ECM), blood microparticle, platelet, and serine-type endopeptidase inhibitor functions. An exploratory Yellow-module-focused analysis identified 10 snoRNAs with nominally lower abundance in CA than in HB (p < 0.05), showing concordant directions of differential abundance with the global analysis. The strength of differential RNA evidence correlated with mean intramodular RNA-protein correlation (Spearman ρ = 0.788, p = 2.85 × 10-6). External snoDB target mapping supported 28.6% of the exploratory network edges, including SNORD38A-FN1, SNORA73B-LAMB1, SNORD22-LAMB1, and SNORD22-NCAM1. Integration of differential plasma snoRNA profiling, cross-omic network analysis, and experimentally observed snoRNA interaction data indicated convergence on ECM/collagen and platelet/coagulation biology. These candidate snoRNA-protein axes may characterize differences in the circulating molecular states of CA and HB.

title: Convergent molecular pathways and shared genetic mechanisms in classic syndromic autism spectrum disorders: a narrative review.
abstract: Autism spectrum disorders (ASD) are defined as a group of neurodevelopmental disorders that share common core features including restrictive repetitive stereotypic behavioral patterns and interests affecting social communication. Over 1,200 genes have been associated with ASD and impacted by copy number variants, chromosomal, and/or single gene defects or epigenetics. Genetic factors contribute to most cases of autism. At least twelve classic genetic disorders with autism as a common feature were selected involving 31 causative or implicated genes with 30 recognized as ASD genes. These disorders were selected to represent a range of genetic abnormalities such as chromosomal deletions, duplications, or trisomy, as well as single or multiple defective genes often with inter-relationship to other genes. Collectively, these syndromes present with neurodevelopmental/behavior/psychiatric findings with ASD, ADHD, intellectual disability and/or psychosis as features. This narrative review is novel by synthesizing available evidence on shared genes, molecular pathways, and protein-protein interaction networks across twelve classic syndromic autism spectrum disorders. Drawing on existing literature and curated web-based databases including STRING and BioGRID, nineteen of the 31 causative and/or implicated genes identified across syndromic autism disorders showed overlap across the twelve classic syndromes having different genetic defects and converged on shared molecular functions, pathways and biological processes. These related to chromatin remodeling, RNA regulation of neurodevelopment and function, synaptic signaling, neuronal connectivity, and protein homeostasis. Phelan-McDermid, Fragile X, Rett, Prader-Willi, Angelman, Burnside-Butler, and Cornelia de Lange syndromes exhibited overlapping pathways related to typical features of autism including social behavior, language acquisition, and associated neurodevelopment. Novel observations of shared molecular patterns across classic genetically distinct syndromes with ASD showed disturbances suggestive of unified, pathway-based therapeutics requiring more investigations to inform future treatment strategies.

title: Ultraconserved Elements Mark Genes Involved in Multilayered Regulation and Human Development.
abstract: Ultraconserved elements (UCEs) are genomic sequences exhibiting exceptional evolutionary conservation across vertebrate taxa, yet their biological functions remain poorly understood. Here, we investigated the functional and expression characteristics of human protein-coding genes containing UCEs. Observed UCE distributions across Gene Ontology and manually curated, mutually exclusive functional groups of genes were compared with 1000 randomized UCE datasets that preserved natural UCE clustering. UCEs are preferentially located within genes involved in multilayered regulation, including transcription, chromatin organization, RNA processing, and ubiquitin-mediated protein regulation, whereas genes associated with membrane, extracellular, structural, transport, and metabolic functions are relatively UCE-poor. Within enriched groups, UCE accumulation is concentrated in multifunctional developmental regulators rather than in constitutive cellular machinery. Compared with length-matched UCE-free controls, UCE-rich genes showed higher and broader expression across 68 adult tissues and significantly higher prenatal expression in all seven organs examined. This expression excess was greatest in the developing brain and cerebellum and was most pronounced during early prenatal development. UCE-rich transcription factors are specifically enriched in developmental and chromatin-regulatory programs, including HOX-related embryonic patterning. These findings indicate that UCEs preferentially mark genes involved in several levels of cellular regulation and link ultraconservation to multilayered gene regulation and early human development.

title: Single-Cell Transcriptomic Analysis Identifies a Translation/RBP-Related Fibroblast Signature for Drug Repurposing in Idiopathic Pulmonary Fibrosis.
abstract: Idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis (IPF) is characterized by persistent fibroblast activation and excessive extracellular matrix deposition. However, transcriptional heterogeneity associated with translation- and RNA-binding protein (RBP)-related processes within IPF fibroblasts remains incompletely characterized. Here, we analyzed two independent human IPF single-cell RNA-sequencing cohorts to identify fibroblast states that differed in Translation/RBP-related transcriptional programs while sharing high fibrotic output. Donor-paired pseudobulk analysis in GSE136831 identified a transcriptional signature distinguishing these states, and genes showing consistent directional changes in the independent GSE135893 cohort were retained to derive a cross-cohort signature. Reverse-connectivity analysis across CLUE, L1000CDS2, and iLINCS was then used to prioritize compounds predicted to transcriptionally oppose this signature. Candidate compounds were subsequently evaluated in transforming growth factor-β1 (TGF-β1)-stimulated human fetal lung fibroblasts (HFL-1), with cell viability, α-smooth muscle actin (α-SMA), and collagen I used for initial phenotypic assessment. PP-1, PK-11195, dabrafenib, GSK-1059615, and dasatinib reduced both profibrotic markers within the tested concentration ranges, identifying them as candidates for further investigation. Together, these findings define a cross-cohort Translation/RBP-related fibroblast signature in IPF and support its use as a transcriptome-guided strategy for prioritizing compounds with antifibrotic phenotypic activity.

title: HMB-Net: Synergizing Latent Sequential Dynamics and Local Sequence Motifs for Robust RNA Methylation Prediction.
abstract: Accurate site-level identification of RNA post-transcriptional modifications is essential for deciphering epitranscriptomic regulation. However, existing deep learning predictors typically rely on either convolutional filters with limited receptive fields or self-attention mechanisms with quadratic complexity, while parallel hybrid networks often struggle to coordinate global sequence context with local motif sensitivity. Here, we present HMB-Net, an interpretable hybrid framework that couples a Selective State Space Model (Mamba) with a deep Bidirectional Long Short-Term Memory (Bi-LSTM) network in a sequential "Latent-to-Motif" hierarchy. Rather than extracting features in parallel, HMB-Net first employs a Mamba encoder to capture long-range sequence dependencies in linear time, which then guides a multi-layer Bi-LSTM to resolve fine-grained motif boundaries, followed by a bidirectional cross-attention module to integrate multi-scale representations. Comprehensive benchmarking across 20 mammalian datasets spanning N6-methyladenosine (m6A), 5-methylcytosine (m5C), and N1-methyladenosine (m1A) modifications in human, mouse, and rat demonstrates that HMB-Net consistently outperforms representative convolutional, recurrent, and Transformer-based baselines. Ablation experiments further confirm the benefit of the global-to-local encoding order over single-branch, reverse-ordered, and parallel dual-branch variants. Moreover, dimensionality reduction and integrated-gradient saliency analyses show that HMB-Net learns well-separated feature representations and autonomously focuses on conserved flanking consensus motifs (such as RRACH) without predefined biochemical rules, providing a reliable computational tool for transcriptome-wide modification mapping.

title: Mitochondrial Genome Architecture of Cephus nigrinus Thomson, 1871 and the Conserved IQM Rearrangement in Cephinae (Hymenoptera: Cephidae).
abstract: Mitochondrial gene rearrangements provide useful characters for investigating genome evolution in Hymenoptera, but mitogenomic sampling within Cephidae remains limited. Here, the mitochondrial genome of Cephus nigrinus Thomson, 1871 was reconstructed from publicly available Illumina whole-genome sequencing data (SRA: SRR23907852) and compared with available cephid mitochondrial genomes. The assembled sequence is 16,782 bp long, has an A + T content of 81.38%, and contains 13 protein-coding genes, 22 transfer RNA genes, and two ribosomal RNA genes. An A + T-rich region of 1295 bp was identified in the deposited annotation. Comparative gene-order analysis revealed a conserved rearrangement of the ancestral mitochondrial IQM cluster, characterized by the positioning of trnQ before trnI near nad2 and the relocation of trnM immediately downstream of rrnS. Phylogenetic analyses based on a concatenated dataset of 13 protein-coding genes, 22 tRNAs, and two rRNAs recovered C. nigrinus and C. pygmeus as sister taxa with strong support. However, the placement of this pair relative to C. cinctus received lower support in the maximum-likelihood analysis. The results expand available mitogenomic information for Cephinae and support conservation of the rearranged mitochondrial gene organization among the examined Cephus species. Further validation is needed to establish the complete structure of the repetitive control region.

title: Resolving the mechanisms on immobilized microspheres enhancing oil cleanup under typical deep-sea conditions via tracing the ecological and evolutionary dynamics of microbial generalists and specialists.
abstract: Deep-sea oil pollution has garnered global concern yet. Immobilization-assisted bioremediation depending on microbial interactions represents a critical strategy for mitigating petroleum contamination. However, the behaviors of bacteria occupying distinct ecological niches during such remediation at deep-sea conditions remain inadequately understood. Herein, via multiple sequencing techniques and biochemical detection, the ecological and evolutionary characteristics of generalists and specialists were tracked under the microsphere-driven bioremediation of oily sediment at deep-sea microcosm. Ecologically, the microspheres increased the diversity of active niche bacteria (RNA-based consortium) in sediment and introduced more stochastic processes into community assembly. Meanwhile, they reinforced the community stability of the two niche taxa by increasing the number of nodes and edges, as well as the robustness of molecular networks in sediment. Genomic analyses revealed the division of labor between generalist and specialist communities. Notably, the microspheres increased the abundance of generalists and specialists that possessed higher gene number associated with petroleum decomposition. Evolutionarily, ecological equilibrium was maintained via a reduced transition rate from specialists to generalists and an elevated diversification rate within specialists. Furthermore, global dataset analysis showed the important niche bacteria activated by the microsphere were widely distributed in the deep sea, indicating the broad applicability of microsphere-based remediation in diverse deepwater habitats. Collectively, the findings highlight that the microspheres likely govern the ecological and evolutionary traits of niche bacteria to improve system stability and function, thereby enhancing oil cleanup. This work provides a novel mechanistic perspective to guide the application and design of microsphere-mediated remediation plan against in-situ pollution.

title: Plant-Derived Biofactors Regulating Biomolecular Condensates: Phytochemical Modulation of Liquid-Liquid Phase Separation in Cellular Function and Disease.
abstract: Biomolecular condensates formed through liquid-liquid phase separation (LLPS) have emerged as central regulators of cellular organization, coordinating key processes such as transcription, ribonucleic acid (RNA) metabolism, and stress responses, while their dysregulation is increasingly recognized as a unifying mechanism underlying diverse pathologies, including neurodegenerative diseases, cancer, viral infections, and inflammatory disorders. Although plant-derived small molecules can alter condensate behavior, their mechanisms of action and therapeutic potential remain poorly defined. Here, we propose an integrative framework for phytochemical modulation of LLPS, distinguishing direct interactions with condensate components from indirect regulation through signaling pathways, post-translational modifications (PTMs), and redox balance. Using representative compounds such as epigallocatechin gallate (EGCG), curcumin, quercetin, and resveratrol, we analyze how phytochemicals influence condensate dynamics in pathological contexts, including protein aggregation, viral assembly, oncogenic transcription, and immune signaling. Importantly, we identify a critical gap between functional observations and quantitative biophysical evidence: most studies lack direct assessment of condensate properties such as material state, dynamics, and phase behavior. We further highlight translational limitations related to poor bioavailability, a lack of standardized LLPS assays, and limited in vivo validation. To address these challenges, we discuss emerging strategies including high-throughput screening approaches and nanocarrier-based delivery systems aimed at enabling precise modulation of condensate dynamics. Collectively, this work positions plant-derived compounds as a promising yet underdeveloped class of modulators of cellular mesoscale organization and provides a conceptual foundation for developing LLPS-targeted phytotherapeutic strategies.

title: Discovery of Two Potential and Novel Toll-like Receptor 7 Antagonists via Molecular Docking, Molecular Dynamics Simulation and In Vitro Biological Evaluation.
abstract: Toll-like receptor 7 (TLR7) is an important pattern recognition receptor. It mainly participates in the recognition of single-stranded RNA and is closely related to various disease processes. In humans, the enormous potential of TLR7 antagonists in reducing inflammation and alleviating autoimmune damage has been identified. Similar effects have also been observed in livestock and poultry. Therefore, using porcine TLR7 as the target, we combined virtual screening with a heterologous reporter gene assay to identify potential ligands, aiming to provide a research basis for the development of immune modulators. The structure of porcine TLR7 was predicted through homology modeling, and molecular docking was performed for virtual screening of potential ligands. ADMET and toxicity properties of small molecules were predicted. Subsequently, a mouse TLR7 reporter cell was employed for in vitro detection of TLR7 activity and cytotoxicity. The interaction modes and molecular dynamics simulations between hit compounds and receptors were further analyzed. The porcine TLR7 structure was predicted by homology modeling. According to the scoring ranking of molecular docking and of ADMET and toxicity prediction, fifty compounds with satisfactory pharmacokinetic properties and safety were screened and their inhibitory effects on R848-induced TLR7 activation were verified. Among them, two hit compounds with novel structures, HY02-35 and HY02-46, exhibited significant mouse TLR7 antagonistic activity. HY02-35, with a parent nucleus structure of 2-indolone, exhibited an inhibitory concentration range between 10.25 and 38.23 µM, with a median estimate of 14.73 µM. The core structure of HY02-46 is 1,4-dihydropyrano [2,3-c] pyrazole, and the IC50 falls between 21.92 and 36.00 µM, with a median estimate of 26.61 µM. The above-mentioned hit compounds had strong interactions with porcine TLR7, formed stable complexes with the receptor, and can significantly reduce the mRNA levels of IFN-β and TNF-α. In short, this study obtained two hit compounds with novel structures and moderate inhibitory activity in vitro. These hits provide a starting point for subsequent structural optimization and in vivo pharmacological studies in porcine subjects.

title: Anticancer Therapy-Induced Alterations in Tumor-Derived Extracellular Vesicles: Molecular Mechanisms and Biological Effects.
abstract: Anticancer treatment alters the secretion and molecular composition of tumor-derived extracellular vesicles (EVs). Chemotherapy, ionizing radiation, and molecularly targeted therapy are associated with changes in EV-associated microRNAs (miRNAs), circular RNAs (circRNAs), long non-coding RNAs (lncRNAs), small nuclear RNAs (snRNAs), proteins, metabolic components, and tumor-associated antigens. Some treatment-associated EV changes are supported by molecular characterization alone, whereas others have been evaluated for functional effects in recipient cells. At the donor-cell level, altered EV release and cargo loading involve RAB family small GTPases, lysosomal degradation, multivesicular body-plasma membrane fusion mediated by soluble N-ethylmaleimide-sensitive factor attachment protein receptor (SNARE) proteins, the exocyst component Exo70, and RNA- and protein-loading processes. In recipient tumor cells, reported responses include changes in WNT/β-catenin and NOTCH signaling, phosphoinositide 3-kinase/protein kinase B (PI3K/AKT), mitogen-activated protein kinase (MAPK), platelet-derived growth factor receptor α (PDGFRα) signaling, glutamine metabolism, and oxidative responses. Evidence supporting individual cargo-response relationships includes both association-based observations and perturbation-based functional validation. In immune cells, C-X-C motif chemokine ligand 1 (CXCL1)-containing EVs increase programmed death-ligand 1 (PD-L1) expression in macrophages, and PD-L1-positive small extracellular vesicles (sEVs) reduce CD8+ T-cell proliferation and granzyme B production, whereas radiation-induced sEVs carrying tumor-associated antigens and heat shock proteins increase antigen presentation and CD4+ and CD8+ T-cell responses. This review separates treatment-associated molecular EV alterations from experimentally evaluated recipient-cell effects to clarify the evidence supporting therapy-induced EV responses.

title: The Complexity and Fuzziness of Conformational Chemistry: Theory and Applications.
abstract: Molecular structure is traditionally described in terms of chemical composition, atomic connectivity, and three-dimensional geometry. However, many molecules, particularly biomacromolecules, exist not as single structures but as dynamic ensembles of interconverting conformers whose populations depend on the surrounding physicochemical context. This work proposes that such conformational ensembles can be interpreted as molecular fuzzy sets, thereby establishing a conceptual bridge between conformational chemistry, information theory, and fuzzy logic. The theoretical framework is introduced by representing molecular structures as adjacency matrices and extending this description to conformational distributions. Experimental evidence is discussed through the photochromic behavior of merocyanines, whose temperature- and environment-dependent conformational distributions encode measurable amounts of fuzzy information. Further support is provided by proteins, DNA, and RNA, where conformational heterogeneity underlies multifunctionality, gene regulation, alternative splicing, molecular recognition, and adaptive cellular responses. Within this perspective, biological function emerges from context-dependent distributions of molecular states rather than from unique static structures. Conformational ensembles are also described as thermalized quantum mixed states, suggesting new links between molecular complexity, fuzzy information processing, and quantum biological phenomena. Finally, the implications of molecular fuzziness for Chemical Artificial Intelligence are discussed, highlighting the possibility of exploiting molecular conformational dynamics as a substrate for adaptive, context-sensitive, and chemically embodied information processing.

title: Construction of a Yeast Two-Hybrid cDNA Library from Soybean Seeds at Different Developmental Stages and Screening of SW16.1 Interacting Proteins.
abstract: Seed weight represents a critical yield-associated quantitative trait in soybean (Glycine max) and is governed by polygenic regulatory networks. Although several seed-weight-related genes have been functionally characterized, the interactome of the major seed-weight determining gene SW16.1 remains largely unexplored. In this study, we constructed a yeast two-hybrid (Y2H) cDNA library using pooled total RNA isolated from developing seeds of the soybean cultivar Nannong 1138-2 covering five key seed-development stages. Using GmSW16.1 (cultivated Nannong 1138-2 allelic) as bait, Y2H screening was performed. Following multi-round screening, Sanger sequencing, and filtering based on functional annotation, 11 candidate interactors assigned to nine distinct functional categories were recovered. Interactions were further verified through point-to-point Y2H assays, quantitative α-galactosidase (α-Gal) activity measurements, and bimolecular fluorescence complementation (BiFC). We confirmed that metallothionein-like protein 4A-related Glyma.18G157800 (GmMT4) and the papain-like cysteine protease Glyma.08G116300 physically interact with both GmSW16.1 and GsSW16.1 (wild soybean N24852). A two-glutamine polymorphism within the PolyQ (polyglutamine) repeat tract of these two allelic proteins did not abolish protein-protein interactions, yet significantly altered their interaction strength toward the above-mentioned partners. Glyma.08G116300 displayed preferential transcript accumulation during soybean seed development, and its transcript abundance differed dynamically between the chromosome segment substitution line CSSL3068 and its cultivated parent Nannong 1138-2 across developmental stages. Heterologous overexpression of this gene in Arabidopsis thaliana significantly increased the 1000-seed weight (by 12-15%) and increased seed length and width. This study delivers a seed-development-specific Y2H library resource for soybean research. We put forward a testable working hypothesis describing a dual-layer regulatory module integrating transcriptional control and direct protein-protein interaction for the GmSW16.1-GmMT4 regulatory node. These findings advance our mechanistic understanding of how natural PolyQ allelic variation shapes soybean seed-weight performance and provides candidate gene materials for soybean molecular design breeding.

title: Carotenoid Metabolism in Plant Stress Adaptation: Pathway Regulation, Flux Distribution, and Stress-Adaptive Functions.
abstract: Carotenoids are plastid-localized isoprenoid metabolites essential for photosynthesis, photoprotection, and plant development. Their metabolism also provides precursors for abscisic acid (ABA), strigolactones (SLs), and diverse apocarotenoids involved in environmental adaptation. Both abiotic and biotic stresses can alter carotenoid biosynthesis, composition, and turnover, although the underlying regulatory mechanisms and physiological consequences vary with stress type. This review examines how carotenoid pathway regulation influences metabolite allocation and stress-adaptive functions, with particular emphasis on the control of precursor supply and metabolic branch points. We discuss the contributions of carotenoid metabolism to ABA-mediated stress responses, photoprotection and redox homeostasis, and signaling by carotenoid-derived metabolites, including zaxinone, β-ionone, β-cyclocitral, and SLs. The distinct and overlapping roles of these processes in abiotic stress adaptation and biotic defense are evaluated, while senescence is considered as a developmental process associated with changes in carotenoid turnover and downstream signaling. We further examine how functional specialization among pathway genes, transcriptional and chromatin regulation, RNA-mediated control, protein stability, and enzyme interactions influence pathway activity. Metabolite feedback and competition for shared precursors, particularly at the methylerythritol 4-phosphate (MEP) and geranylgeranyl diphosphate (GGPP) nodes, provide additional mechanisms for regulating metabolic branch allocation. The reversible interconversion between ABA and ABA glucose ester (ABA-GE) is also discussed as a mechanism of ABA homeostasis distinct from de novo carotenoid-dependent biosynthesis. Importantly, the extent to which changes in metabolite abundance reflect actual flux redistribution remains insufficiently resolved. Future research should therefore prioritize quantitative flux analysis, the mechanisms underlying tissue- and stress-specific regulation, the perception of carotenoid-derived signals, and strategies to improve stress resilience while minimizing growth and yield penalties.

title: MicroRNA Gatekeepers: Integrating Growth, Development, and Stress Adaptation in Cotton.
abstract: As the primary cash crop for natural fiber, cotton develops under sophisticated endogenous genetic programs, with biotic and abiotic stresses continuously driving its adaptive evolution. MicroRNAs (miRNAs) are post-transcriptional regulators that modulate gene expression via target mRNA cleavage, translational repression, and mediation of DNA methylation. miRNAs target transcription factors and hormone signaling pathways to regulate cotton plant architecture and fiber development. In addition, miRNAs mitigate biotic and abiotic stresses through ROS, lignin, and hormone pathways, as well as by forming competing endogenous RNA (ceRNA) modules with long noncoding RNAs (lncRNAs). This review establishes an miRNA-centered regulatory framework that coordinates cotton growth, development, and stress resistance. A series of technologies, including multi-omics combined with machine learning, gene overexpression, STTM, MIM, MIGS, CRISPR editing, foliar dsRNA spraying, and bionanocarriers, are proposed to facilitate the breeding of cotton varieties with high yield, superior fiber quality, and broad-spectrum stress tolerance.

title: Ribonucleases of Very Stable Multi-Protein Complexes from Different Organs of Sea Cucumber Paracaudina chilensis.
abstract: Ribonuclease (RNase) activity, which mediates RNA degradation, plays a critical role in the development and survival of various organisms. In this study, we for the first time performed a comprehensive analysis of ribonuclease activity within highly stable multi-protein complexes isolated from five different organs of the holothurian Paracaudina chilensis (coelomic fluid, body wall, gut, gonads, and respiratory trees). Previously, these complexes were shown to have molecular masses ranging from 1.2 to 1.8 MDa and to differ in their protein-peptide composition. Using zymography, we identified enzymatically active protein bands with apparent molecular masses ranging from approximately 10 to 180 kDa within these complexes, which exhibited RNase activity at pH values from 3.5 to 9.5. The number of detectable activities differed among organs: the greatest diversity (13 distinct RNA-hydrolyzing activities detected under at least one set of conditions) was observed in the complex from coelomic fluid, whereas the complexes from body wall and gut contained the lowest numbers (5 and 6, respectively). Each complex was characterized by a set of RNase catalytic activities that differed in optimal pH (in the presence of 5 mM MgCl2), the number of apparent pH optima per band (from one to four), and sensitivity to metal ions (Mg2+, Mn2+, Zn2+, Co2+, Ca2+, and Ni2+). Some RNase activities were activated by a single metal ion, while others responded to multiple ions. The obtained data demonstrate that preparations of stable multiprotein complexes contain diverse sets of RNA-hydrolyzing activities, but the individual enzymes responsible for these activities remain unidentified. Given the outstanding regenerative capacity of holothurians and the involvement of RNases in the regulation of gene expression and RNA processing, it is suggested that the detected sets of RNase activities may play important roles in tissue regeneration, immune defense, and other physiological processes. This work opens new perspectives for studying the functional role of stable multiprotein complexes in marine invertebrates and highlights the need for further investigation of their catalytic potential.

title: The HDAC-Lactylation Axis in Cancer Chemoresistance: A Metabolic-Epigenetic Interface.
abstract: Chemoresistance remains a critical obstacle in cancer therapy, shaped not only by genetic mutations but also by reversible metabolic and epigenetic adaptations. Enhanced glycolysis and lactate accumulation are associated with tumor fitness before and during therapy and position lactate as more than a metabolic byproduct, enabling it to act as a regulatory metabolite through lysine lactylation of histone and non-histone proteins. This review examines the HDAC-lactylation axis as a metabolic-epigenetic interface and asks whether HDAC-mediated regulation of lactylation causally influences chemotherapy resistance or sensitization. We summarize evidence on lactate production, protein lactylation in cancer, and class I histone deacetylases (HDAC1-3) as delactylases, highlighting the reversible nature of this modification. Current evidence implicates histone and non-histone lactylation in two processes relevant to chemotherapy response: histone lactylation-dependent transcriptional programs involved in metabolic stress responses and phenotypic plasticity, and direct regulation of non-histone proteins involved in DNA repair, RNA processing, genome stability, and cellular stress adaptation. Together, these findings suggest that the HDAC-lactylation axis functions as a dynamic metabolic-epigenetic regulatory network enabling context-dependent adaptive responses. HDAC isoform-focused pharmacological and genetic perturbation, inhibition of lactate dehydrogenase A (LDHA) or monocarboxylate transporter 1 (MCT1), suppression of monocarboxylate transporter 4 (MCT4), and site-specific lactylation proteomics using liquid chromatography-tandem mass spectrometry (LC-MS/MS) could clarify the contribution of this axis to chemotherapy response.

title: CASK Positively Regulates Keratinocyte Proliferation and Modulates the EGFR-ERK-p21 Signaling Axis.
abstract: CASK is a multidomain scaffold protein with diverse cellular functions, but its role in keratinocytes remains unclear. In this study, we established a CASK-silenced human HaCaT keratinocyte model to investigate its biological function. We found that CASK was localized to the plasma membrane, cytosol, and nucleus, and its silencing suppressed keratinocyte proliferation and induced G1-phase arrest. RNA sequencing revealed that CASK depletion attenuates proliferation-associated transcriptional programs. Consistent with this, CASK silencing increased p53 and p21 expression while reducing cyclin B and phosphorylated Rb levels, with elevated p53 and p21 mRNA in shCASK cells. However, CASK silencing-associated p21 upregulation is not majorly dependent on p53 activity. Mechanistically, CASK silencing enhanced serum-induced activation of EGFR and downstream ERK signaling, which were accompanied by increased expression of the EGFR ligands amphiregulin, TGF-α, and epiregulin, indicating augmented autocrine/paracrine EGFR signaling. Pharmacological inhibition studies demonstrated that activation of the EGFR-ERK signaling pathway is essential for p21 upregulation upon CASK silencing. Promoter reporter analyses further revealed that CASK deficiency enhances p21 transcription. Collectively, these findings reveal a previously unrecognized role of CASK in regulating keratinocyte growth and cell-cycle progression. CASK promotes keratinocyte proliferation by restraining autocrine/paracrine EGFR-ERK signaling and suppressing p21 expression, thereby contributing to epidermal homeostasis and growth control.

title: Engineering Lipid Nanoparticles Beyond ApoE-Mediated Liver Tropism: Design Strategies for Extrahepatic and Organ-Selective Delivery.
abstract: Lipid nanoparticles (LNPs) have evolved into a significant delivery technology for nucleic acid therapies, including messenger RNA (mRNA), small interfering RNA (siRNA), and genome editing tools. Although LNPs have demonstrated therapeutic success, they display strong tropism to the liver when systemically delivered, thus restricting their use for targeted delivery to extrahepatic organs. The major factor responsible for the liver targeting of LNPs is the binding of apolipoprotein E (ApoE) to the nanoparticle surface, which enables their recognition by lipoprotein receptors and uptake by liver cells. However, increasing evidence suggests that the tropism of LNPs can be altered by controlling lipid composition, physical and chemical properties, and acquired biological properties. This review discusses the mechanisms responsible for the liver tropism of LNPs as well as recent trends in modulating LNP tropism to extrahepatic organs. How ionizable lipids, helper lipids and sterols, PEG-lipids, LNP properties, and interaction with the protein corona can impact the organ tropism of LNPs as well as approaches for active and endogenous targeting of LNPs for organ- and cell-specific delivery are discussed. The challenges associated with organ- and cell-selective delivery of nucleic acids, such as delivery to functionally specific cell populations, endosomal release, species-specific translation, safety, repeated dosing, and clinical translation, are also described.

title: A Novel NKAP Gene Frameshift Mutation in a Sardinian Family Causes Early Cell Death and Secondary Skewed X-Chromosome Inactivation and Associates with Multiple Male Miscarriages.
abstract: NF-κB-activating protein (NKAP) gene maps to Xq24 and encodes a nuclear protein involved in NF-κB transcription factor activation. Missense variants in NKAP have previously been reported in males with X-linked intellectual disability. Here, we identified a recurrent, novel frameshift variant, c.172del (p.His58Ilefs74*), by targeted X-chromosome sequencing (X-TRS) in seven females from a Sardinian family showing fully skewed X-chromosome inactivation (XCI). To investigate the functional effect of the mutation, we knocked out (KO) and knocked down (KD) NKAP in healthy donor fibroblasts and mouse embryonic stem cells, respectively. We performed RNA sequencing, immunofluorescence, and Western blot analysis on fibroblasts derived from the index subject. We demonstrated that the NKAP frameshift variant leads to monoallelic wild-type (WT) transcription and does not directly affect XCI, indicating secondary rather than primary XCI skewing. NKAP-edited human fibroblasts underwent cell death, leading to the positive selection of WT cells. The NKAP correctly localized to the nucleus but showed reduced expression. We also showed that XIST expression was not affected by this NKAP mutation, further excluding a primary XCI event. Our findings demonstrate that this novel NKAP frameshift variant causes early cell death and post-mitotic negative selection of mutant cells, resulting in a fully secondary XCI. Female carriers are healthy and fertile, whereas affected males are likely nonviable. In conclusion, our results provide insights into both the role of NKAP in cells and novel clinical implications for human fertility.

title: TLR7 Deficiency Reveals Compartment-Specific Respiratory-Systemic Immune Responses During Severe Influenza A Virus Infection.
abstract: Influenza A virus (IAV) infection can progress from a localized respiratory illness to severe disease characterized by pulmonary inflammation, systemic cytokinemia, acute-phase responses and multi-organ pathology. Toll-like receptor 7 (TLR7) is a key sensor of viral single-stranded RNA and an important component of antiviral immunity; however, its role in extending immunity from the respiratory tract to peripheral compartments during severe IAV infection remains incompletely understood. Here, we investigated the relationship between TLR7 and innate, cellular and humoral immune responses across respiratory and peripheral compartments during IAV infection. Using TLR7-deficient mice infected with the highly pathogenic PR8 H1N1 strain, we profiled immune responses in nasal tissue, bronchoalveolar lavage fluid, lung, blood and spleen, together with cytokine production, C-reactive protein levels, T cell activation and antibody isotype responses. Loss of TLR7 was accompanied by compartment-specific alterations in innate immunity, including differences in pulmonary macrophage and dendritic cell responses, and altered plasmacytoid dendritic cell distribution across respiratory and peripheral compartments. Reduced virus-specific CD8+ T cell expansion, lower IFNγ and TNFα production by T cells, and diminished circulating inflammatory cytokines and C-reactive protein were also observed. In parallel, altered humoral responses included reduced mucosal IgA, systemic IgM and Th1-associated IgG2a responses, together with changes in antibody isotype distribution. Collectively, these findings demonstrate that TLR7 deficiency is associated with broad, compartment-specific alterations in innate and adaptive immune responses during established IAV infection, extending across the respiratory tract, blood and spleen and correlating with disease severity. These findings support a role for TLR7-associated signaling in shaping the broader respiratory-systemic immune response, with its presence linked to both antiviral immune engagement and the magnitude of systemic inflammation during severe IAV infection.

title: Host Factor ANP32A in Avian Influenza Virus Replication and Cross-Species Adaptation: A Narrative Review.
abstract: Highly pathogenic avian influenza virus undergoes continuous evolution with strengthened cross-species transmission capacity, posing a severe threat to global public health security. Host acidic nuclear phosphoprotein 32A (ANP32A) acts as a critical host cofactor for activating influenza viral RNA-dependent RNA polymerase, and plays a central role in viral replication and host adaptation. This review systematically elaborates the molecular features of ANP32A, as well as the mechanism by which its leucine-rich repeat (LRR) domain specifically binds to the polymerase basic protein 2 (PB2) subunit and its low-complexity acidic region (LCAR) interacts with polymerase acidic protein (PA) to facilitate the assembly and functional activation of viral polymerase complexes. It also summarizes the influences of species-specific sequence variations and splicing isoforms of ANP32A on the host restriction barrier of cross-species transmission. Further analyses reveal that ANP32A indirectly modulates the transcriptional levels of genes related to interferons, NF-κB and NOD-like receptor pyrin domain-containing 3 (NLRP3) inflammasomes via chromatin epigenetic modification and transcriptional resource competition, remodeling the cellular antiviral microenvironment as a nuclear transcriptional regulator. ANP32A and acidic nuclear phosphoprotein 32B (ANP32B) exert complementary functions to support viral polymerase activity, while acidic nuclear phosphoprotein 32E (ANP32E) only provides weak auxiliary effects on a small subset of mutant influenza strains with its primary physiological function centered on chromatin regulation; the three proteins jointly participate in the regulatory network of viral replication. Drawing on recent advances in cryo-electron microscopy structural biology and CRISPR/Cas9 gene-editing technologies, which are discussed narratively in this review, this review highlights the pivotal hub role of ANP32A in viral host adaptation and cross-species spillover.

title: From Effusion to Diagnosis: Integrating the FIP Effusion Index and Cell Tube Block Immunohistochemistry in a Geriatric Cat.
abstract: Feline infectious peritonitis (FIP) can be overlooked in older cats with competing causes of effusion. An older female domestic shorthair cat with hyperthyroidism and a hypertrophic cardiomyopathy phenotype developed abdominal effusion in December 2023. Initial effusion total protein was 5.46 g/dL, the albumin-to-globulin ratio was 0.48 and delta total nucleated cell ratio (ΔTNC) was 60.58, yielding a retrospectively calculated FIP Effusion Index of 126.2. Coronavirus RT-PCR detected FCoV RNA, with M1058L mutation positivity, and cell tube block immunohistochemistry (CTB-IHC) demonstrated viral antigen within macrophages. A second sample collected from scant residual effusion 9 days after the initiation of GS-441524 had a ΔTNC of 2.15 and a FIP Effusion Index of 7.17, despite a higher total protein concentration and a lower albumin-to-globulin ratio. GS-441524 treatment began on 20 December 2023 and ended on 22 March 2024. Abdominal fluid was no longer detected at the assessment on 25 January. No confirmed FIP relapse was documented before death during cardiopulmonary decompensation in January 2026. This case illustrates complementary contributions of the FIP Effusion Index and CTB-IHC, with an exploratory observation of serial FIP Effusion Index change. Threshold comparison is retrospective. The lower index was observed during treatment alongside markedly reduced effusion, but this observation does not establish a treatment effect or validate treatment monitoring.

title: Geminivirus Suppressor Proteins: Targeting Host DNA Methylation Machinery.
abstract: Geminiviruses are a large family of DNA viruses that are a major threat to agricultural biosecurity. They are obligate pathogens that replicate using Rolling circle replication (RCR). During RCR, their double-stranded DNA intermediates become targets of host-mediated RNA-dependent DNA methylation (RdDM), an important epigenetic antiviral defense mechanism. However, geminiviruses encode multifunctional proteins that suppress and counteract transcriptional gene silencing. This review examines four geminiviral multifunctional proteins, the replication-associated protein (C1), the transcriptional activator protein (C2), the movement protein (V2), and the C4 protein, that suppress DNA methylation. These viral proteins interfere with DNA methylation through several mechanisms, including disrupting key components such as Argonaute 4 (AGO4) and Domain Rearranged Methylase 2 (DRM2); repressing methylation-associated genes transcriptionally; and indirectly hindering SAM production by disrupting the methyl cycle. Despite these advances, the mechanism by which DNA methylation restricts viral gene expression and may limit viral replication remains poorly understood. The interplay between geminviruses and host RdDM exemplifies a molecular arms race, in which RdDM serves as a critical defense actively targeted by geminvirus suppressor proteins.

title: Characterization and Comparative Analysis of Complete Chloroplast Genome of Vachellia tortilis subsp. tortilis (Fabaceae).
abstract: The Vachellia tortilis subsp. tortilis is a dryland tree included in the Fabaceae family. The genus Vachellia includes 164 species, 38 subspecies, and 25 varieties. The taxonomic placement of Vachellia has historically been unstable; the genus was only recently segregated from Acacia. In this study, we sequenced and characterized the chloroplast genome of V. tortilis subsp. tortilis and compared it with those of related species. The total chloroplast genome length of V. tortilis subsp. tortilis was 164,956 bp, and it contained 132 genes: 87 protein-coding genes, eight ribosomal RNA genes, and 37 transfer RNA genes. Simple repeat analysis showed that the chloroplast genome of V. tortilis subsp. tortilis contained 273 repeats. Codon usage bias analysis showed that the chloroplast genome of V. tortilis subsp. tortilis encoded 24,633 codons. The phylogenetic analysis revealed two distinct clades in the genus Vachellia: the first comprises V. tortilis subsp. tortilis and Vachellia tortilis subsp. raddiana, while the second includes Vachellia flava, Vachellia seyal, and Vachellia nilotica. This study improves knowledge of evolutionary relationships in the genus Vachellia and provides valuable genetic resources.

title: Tumour Cell-Associated Heterogeneity in Antiviral Immunity Shapes Influenza Responses and Immune-Modulatory Signalling in Lung Cancer.
abstract: Respiratory viral infections occur within the same anatomical niche as lung cancer, yet how lung cancer cells respond to infection and how these responses influence antiviral and inflammatory signalling remain poorly understood. This study investigated innate immune responses to influenza A virus (IAV) infection across a panel of lung epithelial cell lines. Non-malignant bronchial epithelial and non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC) cell lines representing adenocarcinoma and squamous cell carcinoma were infected with IAV. Antiviral and inflammatory gene expression, viral RNA and protein detection, infection-induced cell death, pattern recognition receptor expression, and immune checkpoint ligand expression were assessed using molecular, biochemical and flow cytometric approaches. Interferon (IFN) receptor blockade and mitochondrial reactive oxygen species scavenging were used to investigate selected signalling mechanisms. NSCLC cell lines exhibited heterogeneous innate immune responses to IAV infection, with differential regulation of RNA-sensing pathways and canonical antiviral signalling components. Although IFN responses were retained, NSCLC cells exhibited reduced infection-induced apoptosis and prolonged viral RNA and protein detection compared with non-malignant epithelial cells. IAV infection was also associated with changes in DNA-sensing receptor expression, including TLR9, and increased expression of the immune checkpoint ligand PD-L1. These findings identify substantial cell line-associated heterogeneity in antiviral responses to IAV across lung epithelial cell lines, including NSCLC cells. The observed differences in viral RNA and protein detection, cell death responses and immune-modulatory signalling provide a framework for understanding how respiratory viral infections may interact with lung cancer cells to shape antiviral and inflammatory responses within the tumour environment.

title: Adhesion G protein-coupled receptor A2 promotes tick-borne encephalitis virus replication by interacting with NS2B to enhance viral protease activity.
abstract: Tick-borne encephalitis virus (TBEV) is a neurotropic flavivirus that causes severe neurological disease in humans, but the host factors required for its efficient replication remain incompletely understood. Here, we identify ADGRA2 as a novel host dependency factor for TBEV. Loss of ADGRA2, but not other ADGR family members, markedly restricts infection by multiple TBEV strains in human cells and primary mouse astrocytes. ADGRA2 is dispensable for viral entry but is required for efficient viral RNA replication, as demonstrated by impaired negative-strand RNA synthesis and accumulation of double-stranded RNA intermediates in ADGRA2-deficient cells. During infection, ADGRA2 is relocalized from the plasma membrane to the endoplasmic reticulum, where it functions independently of canonical WNT/β-catenin signaling. Mechanistically, ADGRA2 interacts with the viral cofactor NS2B, enhances NS2B-NS3 autocleavage and protease activity, promotes viral polyprotein processing, and facilitates NS2B/NS3 association with NS2A to enhance replication organelle biogenesis. ADGRA2 also promotes replication of Japanese encephalitis virus (JEV), Zika virus (ZIKV) and Dengue virus serotype 2 (DENV-2), suggesting a conserved role across flaviviruses. Together, these findings reveal that a host membrane receptor can be repurposed to drive NS2B-dependent protease maturation and replication complex assembly, thereby enabling efficient flaviviral replication.

title: Toward precision nanomedicine via artificial intelligence guided design and prediction.
abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) is advancing nanomedicine development by linking formulation variables and biological context with delivery, therapeutic efficacy, and safety. This review examines AI assisted formulation design, centralized formulation databases, prediction of nanoparticle self assembly, and models of cell and tissue selective delivery, biodistribution, and therapeutic outcomes. Recent advances in predicting nanotoxicity and nanoparticle induced immune responses further emphasize the importance of incorporating safety endpoints into nanomedicine optimization. Beyond nanocarrier engineering, foundation models and multimodal analyses of single-cell and spatial data are expanding biological discovery by characterizing disease associated cellular states, prioritizing therapeutic targets, and predicting treatment responses. Computational approaches also support the design of therapeutic RNA, peptides, proteins, and programmable protein nanomaterials. For example, mRNA sequences generated by GEMORNA and delivered via lipid nanoparticles increased erythropoietin expression in mice by up to 15-fold compared with a benchmark sequence. Integration of biological discovery with biomolecular and nanocarrier design may inform therapeutic cargo selection, targeting strategies, and functional nanomaterial development. AI may connect patient specific biological characteristics with predictions of nanomedicine delivery and therapeutic response to support patient stratification and individualized treatment selection. Integration of histological, imaging, molecular, and longitudinal data may enable treatment strategies to be adapted to differences in tissue characteristics, disease state, and therapeutic response. Emerging approaches based on digital twins and adaptive treatment control may extend the framework toward individualized dosing and dynamic treatment optimization. Major challenges include data heterogeneity, limited model generalizability, and the need for experimental and prospective validation. Progress toward precision therapy will require integrated frameworks that jointly consider delivery, efficacy, selectivity, and safety while clearly distinguishing demonstrated applications from future opportunities.

title: Host-derived lipids license proliferation of cholesterol-auxotrophic tick cells and promote flavivirus output.
abstract: Sterol molecules play indispensable roles in the biology of cells and organisms. Yet, arthropods, including ticks, lack the capacity for de novo sterol biosynthesis and must rely on exogenous sources. How these organisms sense and utilise exogenous sterols at the cellular level remains only partially understood. Here, using the tick Ixodes ricinus IRE/CTVM19 cells cultured with full serum, or lipoprotein-deficient serum (LPDS), we found that LPDS supplementation arrested cellular proliferation. Defined lipid add-backs, cholesterol and linoleic acid, restored proliferation. After internalisation, tick cells exhibited a non-canonical cholesterol distribution, with free cholesterol accumulating predominantly within lysosomes and lipid droplets, and only marginally in plasma membrane. Availability of serum lipids also altered the expression of genes involved in lysosomal cholesterol handling, including specific niemann-pick C2 (npc2) and lysosomal integral membrane protein 2 (limp-2) transcripts. Consistent with a functional role for lysosomal trafficking, pharmacological disruption of lysosomal acidification or cholesterol export disturbed sub-cellular partitioning of cholesterol and inhibited cell proliferation. Finally, we examined whether serum lipid availability affected tick-borne encephalitis virus (TBEV) infection. While the LPDS culture did not significantly alter cellular TBEV RNA, it reduced levels of extracellular TBEV RNA. Together, these findings identify cholesterol and linoleic acid as selective extracellular inputs that enable proliferative competence and reveal serum lipoprotein availability as a determinant of extracellular TBEV RNA production.

title: Vacuolar aquaporin TIP1;1 binding with small auxin-up RNA 30 influences Arabidopsis cold responses.
abstract: Cold stress is a major threat for global food security impacting agricultural productivity by influencing cellular processes including photosynthetic efficiency, nutrient and water translocation in plants. Plant response to cold stress involves the regulation of complex transcriptional networks, including the SMALL AUXIN UPREGULATED RNA (SAUR) gene family. Canonically, SAURs inhibit clade PROTEIN PHOSPHATASE 2C, CLADE D (PP2C.D) phosphatases for control of plasma membrane H+-ATPase phosphorylation and activity. The plasma membrane H+-ATPases are primary transporters energizing osmotic ion and water transport across plant cell membranes. Here we uncover unexpected mechanisms involving SAUR30 protein in cold stress response that encompass both transcriptional regulation and post translational control to influence cold sensitivity in plants. Using yeast two-hybrid and mating-based split-ubiquitin screens, ratio BiFC, Xenopus oocyte swelling assays, and Arabidopsis loss-of-function/overexpression lines, we show that under cold stress, increased SAUR30 abundance downregulates aquaporin TONOPLAST INTRINSIC PROTEIN 1;1 (TIP1;1) expression. Remarkably, we found that SAUR30 interacts with TIP1;1 resulting in suppression of TIP1;1 water channel activity. Physiologically, disrupting this interaction-either by saur30 knockout or by expressing a non-binding SAUR30 chimera, restores root elongation and cellular water content under cold stress. We propose that cold-induced SAUR30 restricts vacuolar water transport by suppressing both the abundance and the intrinsic activity of TIP1;1, thereby modulating plant growth and cold resilience.

title: First high-resolution structure of the nucleoprotein from the emerging human pathogen Songling virus.
abstract: The Songling virus (SGLV) is a recently discovered tick-borne orthonairovirus with pathogenic potential for humans. Its nucleoprotein (N) is essential for genome packaging and immune evasion, yet its structure remains entirely unexplored. Crucially, SGLV N shares a very low sequence identity with characterized homologs, hindering functional predictions. Here, we present the first high-resolution (2.0 Å) crystal structure of SGLV N. The SGLV N structure comprises a globular head and an elongated stalk domain. The asymmetric unit reveals a structurally conserved head-to-tail dimerization interface. The stalk domain exhibits significant conformational plasticity, evidenced by a 10° tilt between monomers, suggesting a flexible hinge for ribonucleoprotein assembly. Small-angle X-ray scattering (SAXS) confirms that SGLV N remains a compact monomer in solution. We mapped an extended, positively charged RNA-binding groove. Molecular dynamics simulations pinpointed key anchoring residues and relaxed the structure to perfectly match the SAXS data, confirming its biological relevance. Structural comparisons with homologous structures reveal that SGLV N likely harbors an intrinsic endonuclease active site and a caspase-3 cleavage site. These findings provide a crucial foundation for understanding the replication mechanisms of this emerging pathogen and highlight conserved N-protein interfaces as promising targets for future antiviral strategies.

title: 14-3-3ε Facilitates Replication of Multiple Viruses Accompanied by Reduced NF-κB Pathway Activity in Largemouth Bass (Micropterus salmoides).
abstract: Frequent outbreaks of viral diseases and the increasing prevalence of polyviral co-infections have severely constrained the sustainable development of largemouth bass (Micropterus salmoides) aquaculture. Identifying conserved host factors exploited by diverse viruses is critical for developing broad-spectrum antiviral strategies, yet the key host molecules underlying cross-viral infection susceptibility in teleosts remain poorly characterized. Here, this research identifies Micropterus salmoides 14-3-3ε protein (Ms14-3-3ε) as a critical pro-viral host factor that facilitates the replication of multiple phylogenetically distinct viruses by negatively modulating NF-κB-mediated inflammatory responses. Ms14-3-3ε was ubiquitously expressed in healthy largemouth bass tissues and was significantly upregulated both in vivo and in vitro upon infection with viral hemorrhagic septicemia virus (VHSV), largemouth bass virus (LMBV), and red-spotted grouper nervous necrosis virus (RGNNV). Functional gain- and loss-of-function assays demonstrated that Ms14-3-3ε serves as a broad-spectrum pro-viral factor: its overexpression markedly enhanced the transcription and protein expression of core viral genes, whereas Ms14-3-3ε knockdown effectively suppressed the transcription expression of all three viruses and protein levels of VHSV G and RGNNV CP. Mechanistically, Ms14-3-3ε negatively regulates the NF-κB signaling pathway in a dose-dependent manner by specifically inhibiting the phosphorylation of p65 at the Ser536 residue. This suppression further downregulates the expression of downstream pro-inflammatory effector genes NLRP3 and IL-1β, thereby blunting host innate immune defense responses to multi-viral proliferation. Collectively, the results demonstrate that Ms14-3-3ε facilitates the replication of taxonomically distinct fish RNA and DNA viruses associated with reduced NF-κB pathway activity in largemouth bass. This study provides a novel, conserved host target for the development of broad-spectrum antiviral strategies in aquaculture.

title: Group structure dominates pooled peak-gene associations in single-cell multi-omics.
abstract: Peak-gene associations in paired single-cell RNA and chromatin-accessibility (multiome) data are usually nominated by correlating peak accessibility with the expression of a nearby gene across all cells. Such datasets combine discrete groups cell lines, donors, cell types, treatments and libraries that differ in both modalities, so a pooled correlation mixes covariation between groups with covariation within them. We quantified this mixture in a six-line prostate cancer multiome dataset with drug perturbations and in a 15-donor human cortex dataset. Every candidate pair within ± 250 kb of a transcription start site was scored by pooled Pearson correlation and by a fixed-effect combination of within-group correlations, and the resulting calls were decomposed into pooled-only, within-only and shared sets. Calibration used label permutation on the same pairs and a matched trans null in which each cis peak is replaced by an accessibility-matched peak on another chromosome. In the prostate data, 5,624 of 5,631 pooled calls (99.9%) were not supported within cell lines, and the result held across thresholds, windows, minimum-cell filters, and line × treatment, line × library and treatment-specific designs (89-99.9%). Pooled calls were nevertheless 3.2-fold enriched over the matched trans background and skewed towards positive correlation, indicating cis-specific co-variation that differs between lines through regulation or, in cancer cell lines, copy-number differences rather than within them; within-line calls did not exceed the trans background. In the cortex, controlling for donor left most pooled calls supported (21.2% not supported), whereas controlling for cell type left 99.8% unsupported, and donor-controlled calls remained cis-enriched. In a within-line drug-response analysis, a between-line resistant-versus-sensitive contrast was only weakly correlated with treatment response. Pooled peak-gene calls should therefore be read as candidate associations whose level of variation must be stated, and we provide a reproducible protocol for doing so.

title: Lipid metabolism and pediatric tuberculous meningitis: Revealing mechanisms and new directions for diagnosis and treatment.
abstract: Pediatric tuberculous meningitis (TBM), a fatal Mycobacterium tuberculosis infection, causes severe neurological damage. Current diagnostics (clinical signs, CSF analysis, imaging) are often delayed or inaccurate. Emerging evidence links lipid metabolism dysregulation to TBM pathogenesis, though mechanisms remain unclear. (1) Firstly, we exploratorily performed RNA sequencing on peripheral blood from 3 pediatric TBM patients with 7 healthy control data obtained from a public GEO dataset (GSE159337) to identify 7,595 differentially expressed genes (DEGs). 3,763 upregulated genes enriched metabolic pathways, endocytosis, and MAPK signaling, while 3,832 downregulated genes linked to TGF-β signaling. Gene ontology emphasized immune responses, particularly neutrophil activation. Protein-protein interaction networks identified 41 hub genes, including CD274, TGFB1, and MMP9, with TGFB1, JUN, CD274, and MMP9 showing strong lipid metabolism correlations, suggesting a lipid-TBM risk nexus. (2) Furthermore, we validated four of these hub genes (FCGR3B, SPI1, ITGAX, MMP9) in an independent publicly available pediatric TBM study of high quality (GEO GSE111459) via ROC curve and logistic regression analysis. (3) Finally, the expression of these four hub genes were measured by qRT-PCR in an expanded set of clinical samples (13 additional TBM patients vs 12 healthy controls), confirming significantly elevated MMP9 and FCGR3B in TBM (P<0.01). This study suggests that lipid metabolism plays a role in the pathogenesis of pediatric TBM, proposing hub genes and pathways that could serve as potential supporting targets for diagnostics and therapies.

title: Identification of QTLs and candidate genes associated with seed germination capacity under heat stress in watermelon.
abstract: Heat stress (HS) severely inhibits seed germination of direct-seeded crops such as watermelon. However, the genetic basis governing germination capacity under HS remains largely unclear. An F2 population consisting of 132 individuals was developed from a cross between the heat-tolerant inbred line 8R098 (high germination under HS) and the heat-sensitive line 8R122 (low germination under HS). SNP-trait association analysis and linkage mapping were employed to dissect the genetic basis of seed germination capacity under HS. Germination-stage RNA-seq of high- and low-germination accessions under HS was performed to screen the DEGs. Heat tolerance for seed germination segregated at a high-to-low ratio of 1: 3, indicating a nearly recessive genetic nature. A major QTL for HS germination tolerance was fine-mapped to the interval of 29.05~33.41 Mb on chromosome 10, harboring 472 annotated genes. RNA-seq identified 1,519 HS-responsive DEGs enriched in plant hormone signal transduction and metabolic pathways. A total of 101 putative functional non-synonymous SNPs (nsSNPs) were found in 76 protein-coding genes within this QTL region. Integrative analysis of DEGs and nsSNP-containing genes, followed by filtering genes with inconsistent expression trends, retained four candidate genes with allelic variations, namely Cla97C10G205480, Cla97C10G205850, Cla97C10G204760, and Cla97C10G203920. Our findings reveal candidate genes regulating thermotolerance during watermelon seed germination and provide useful genetic resources for breeding watermelon varieties with improved heat tolerance at the germination stage.

title: Genome-Wide Identification of the NAC Gene Family and Expression Analysis Under Contrasting Salinity in Zostera marina L.
abstract: Eelgrass (Zostera marina L.) is a marine angiosperm exposed to substantial salinity fluctuations, yet the transcriptional mechanisms associated with its salinity adaptation responses remain incompletely understood. To characterize the NAC transcription factor family and its potential involvement in salinity responses, we performed genome-wide identification, phylogenetic, structural, duplication, promoter, and expression analyses in Z. marina, followed by quantitative reverse transcription PCR (qRT-PCR) validation. Sixty-three ZmNAC genes were identified and classified into six phylogenetic groups. Most encoded proteins contained a conserved N-terminal NAC domain but varied considerably in length, motif composition, gene structure, and predicted subcellular localization. Duplication analysis classified 55 genes as dispersed duplicates, seven as whole-genome duplication (WGD) or segmental duplicates, and one as a proximal duplicate. Promoter analysis identified 64 cis-acting element types associated mainly with light, phytohormone, and stress responses. RNA-seq analysis of roots, stems, and leaves after 24 h at NaCl concentrations of 0‱, 24‱, and 40‱ revealed distinct salinity- and tissue-dependent expression patterns among the ZmNAC family members. Expression patterns of four candidate genes in leaves, assessed by qRT-PCR, were largely consistent with the RNA-seq results. These findings reveal structural and expression diversification within the ZmNAC family and identify candidate genes for further functional investigation of salinity responses in eelgrass.

title: Neighborhood Competition Correlates with Height-Diameter Growth Allocation and Gene Expression in Clonal Eucalyptus urophylla × E. grandis Plantation.
abstract: Height-diameter (H-D) growth patterns describe the relative growth of tree height and stem diameter and may vary with local competitive conditions. We examined a Eucalyptus urophylla × E. grandis clone DH32-29 plantation across 12 stand units. Phenotypic comparisons included 364 interior trees and 254 true stand-edge trees; RNA-seq was conducted on a balanced subset of 72 trees (36 interior and 36 edge trees), not on the full phenotypic sample. Neighborhood competition around interior trees was characterized using the Hegyi index and basal area in larger trees (BAL), and growth traits were compared between interior and edge trees. Hegyi and BAL were negatively associated with growth, with stronger associations for diameter increment than for height increment. Unadjusted comparisons suggested different growth patterns, but plot-adjusted sensitivity analysis supported differences only in diameter increment and H/D. WGCNA identified modules associated with individual allometric traits, and XGBoost prioritized expression features with moderate model performance (R2 = 0.404). qRT-PCR supported expression trends for selected genes but did not test gene function. These observational results identify associations among neighborhood structure, growth patterns, and gene-expression variation; edge contrasts may also reflect differences in light, wind exposure, microclimate, or soil conditions. The candidate modules and genes require independent and functional validation.

title: Effects of Exogenous Melatonin Concentration on Salt Stress Alleviation in Salix matsudana × S. alba Assessed Through Integrated Physiological Evaluation and Transcriptomic Analysis.
abstract: Salt stress limits the establishment of Salix matsudana × S. alba seedlings. Exogenous melatonin (MT) can alleviate plant salt stress, but its concentration-dependent effects in Salix matsudana × S. alba remain insufficiently characterized. In this study, physiological responses were assessed across three NaCl levels and five MT concentrations, followed by transcriptome analysis of representative treatments. Under 6‱ NaCl, 0.5 mmol L-1 MT significantly reduced relative electrolyte conductivity and malondialdehyde content across three sampling times and increased total chlorophyll, proline, and soluble protein contents and antioxidant enzyme activities at the final sampling relative to the salt-only treatment. An integrated physiological assessment based on principal component analysis and supported by correlation analysis ranked 0.5 mmol L-1 highest under 6‱ NaCl, with 0.3 mmol L-1 ranking second, whereas 1.0 mmol L-1 generally provided no further overall improvement. Compared with the untreated control, the 6‱ NaCl plus 0.5 mmol L-1 MT treatment showed transcriptional changes involving plant hormone signal transduction and starch and sucrose metabolism. Quantitative reverse transcription PCR broadly supported RNA sequencing trends for nine candidate genes. These findings demonstrate concentration-dependent physiological protection and identify candidate pathways for investigating MT-associated salt stress alleviation in hybrid willow.

title: Chronic Stress Attenuates the Glucocorticoid Receptor Transcriptional Programme in the Danio rerio Telencephalon.
abstract: We reanalysed public RNA-seq data from the telencephalon of adult zebrafish after 14 days of chronic unpredictable stress. The deposited runs concatenate pooled libraries, hiding the replicates; we recovered the library boundaries from the block structure of unaligned reads and realigned to GRCz11 with splicing enabled. Unique alignment rose from 63.7-64.2% to 80.6-81.6%, and 275 genes were differentially expressed (FDR < 0.05), 101 of the 155 reported previously and 174 new, with effect sizes matching the published ones (ρ = 0.754). Against gene sets from an nr3c1 knockout, the data show a coordinated, mirror-symmetric shift in receptor-dependent transcription-the receptor-induced set down, the receptor-repressed set up (p ≈ 0.001 for both)-while the original study reported cortisol at control level; "receptor-dependent" denotes set membership, not receptor occupancy. Two artefacts constrain the reading of individual genes: epidermal content differs between groups while neuronal content does not, and the gene list is clustered in the genome far beyond chance. Removing the 85 flagged genes (of 275) leaves the receptor-level result intact (p = 0.0008 and 0.0014) but withdraws the conclusions on keratins and barrier structures. That removal addresses gene-level artefact, not sample composition, which six libraries cannot settle: a between-group difference in tissue composition remains an alternative explanation.

title: Analysis of the Use of shRNA in Atherosclerosis Therapy: Current Status.
