abstract: Atherosclerosis remains the principal pathological substrate of myocardial infarction, ischemic stroke and peripheral artery disease, and its progression is driven by an interlocking set of processes, including hepatic and vascular lipid metabolism, chronic vascular inflammation, macrophage foam cell formation and vascular smooth muscle cell (VSMC) proliferation, none of which is fully controlled by currently approved pharmacotherapy. Short hairpin RNA (shRNA) technology, in which a DNA template encoding a stem-loop transcript is delivered to a cell and processed intracellularly into small interfering RNAs (siRNAs) that trigger sequence-specific mRNA degradation, offers a route to durable, vector-encoded gene silencing that is mechanistically distinct from transiently acting synthetic siRNA or antisense oligonucleotides and that, although non-permanent at the level of the target gene, is not readily reversible at the level of the vector, which cannot easily be withdrawn once administered. This review analyzes the current status of shRNA-based strategies for atherosclerosis therapy. We summarize the molecular mechanism and vector design principles of shRNA-mediated RNA interference (RNAi); critically examine preclinical studies in which shRNA delivered by lentiviral or adeno-associated viral (AAV) vectors has been used to silence hepatic lipid-metabolism genes (PCSK9, ApoB,), the endothelial gene ANGPTL2, inflammasome and inflammatory mediators (NLRP3, TACE/ADAM17), and genes driving VSMC proliferation in restenosis models (connexin 43); we explicitly distinguish this direct shRNA evidence from complementary target-validation studies that use antisense oligonucleotides (e.g., ANGPTL4), synthetic siRNA, genetic knockout, or antimiR approaches (e.g., lncRNA AK136714, CD36, miR-33, P2X7R); and discuss the principal delivery vectors, their tissue tropism, and the toxicity arising from saturation of the endogenous microRNA-processing machinery. We further place shRNA in the context of competing and complementary RNA-based and gene-editing modalities, including clinically approved synthetic siRNA drugs (inclisiran, patisiran) and CRISPR-based gene editing of PCSK9 and ANGPTL3, both of which have now yielded human phase 1 data, to clarify why, despite two decades of robust preclinical proof-of-concept, no shRNA construct has yet reached clinical use in atherosclerosis; we further compare this with the clinical trajectory of vector-encoded shRNA in other indications, in which anti-CCR5 and anti-HCV constructs have already been administered to patients in phase 1/2 trials, in order to establish that the limiting factor is not the hairpin itself but the risk-benefit case obtainable in a chronic, largely asymptomatic disease for which withdrawable and outcome-validated therapies already exist. We conclude that shRNA remains a mechanistically attractive but clinically immature modality whose translation will depend on vector engineering that limits off-target saturation of the RNAi pathway and achieves durable, cell type-restricted expression in the liver, endothelium, macrophages or vascular wall, and, equally, on the identification of an atherosclerosis indication-most plausibly a small, high-residual-risk or locally treatable population-in which durability outweighs the vector-level irreversibility, immunogenicity and manufacturing burden of a viral vector.

title: Cross-Species and Cell-Type-Specific H3K27ac Dynamics Link Brain Aging to Alzheimer's Disease Genes.
abstract: Active H3K27ac marks are dynamically remodelled during brain aging, but their cell-type-specific regulatory roles remain unclear. We integrated genome-wide H3K27ac profiles and transcriptomes from aging Drosophila heads, mouse NeuN+ forebrain neurons, and human NeuN+/NeuN- frontal cortex cells. In Drosophila, age-gained differential (Δ) H3K4me1 and H3K27ac peaks were associated with RNA processing and immune response genes, respectively, suggesting distinct regulatory programs. Despite limited biological replicates, mouse analyses revealed a strong association between promoter-associated ΔH3K27ac and synaptic gene expression in young neurons. Age-related gene-body H3K27ac loss coincided with increased expression of genes involved in GTPase signalling and vesicular transport. In humans (n = 29), NeuN- cells exhibited more age-associated ΔH3K27ac alterations than NeuN+ cells. Genes associated with age-gained peaks were enriched for gliogenesis and amyloid precursor protein metabolic processes, while age-related transcriptional changes associated positively with super-enhancer activity. Comparison with pan-tissue aging signatures revealed shared and cell-type-specific age-related ΔH3K27ac patterns in NeuN+ and NeuN- cells. Integrative analyses showed that age-gained ΔH3K27ac peaks in NeuN- cells overlapped with AD-associated ΔH3K27ac peaks, differentially expressed AD genes, and AD GWAS-linked variants, including those mapped to BIN1 and CR1. These findings highlight extensive H3K27ac remodelling in aging NeuN- cells and its convergence with AD-associated molecular alterations.

title: Advances in Biomarker Discovery for Early Ovarian Cancer Diagnosis.
abstract: Ovarian cancer is one of the deadliest gynecological cancers worldwide. One promising therapeutic approach is the use of combined biomarkers. The Risk of Ovarian Malignancy Algorithm (ROMA) which combines CA125 with Human Epididymal Protein 4 (HE4) is an example of combining biomarkers to gain an optimal predictive outcome. Tumor Protein p53 (TP53) is a transcription factor with tumor suppressor properties. Mutations in TP53 constitute the most frequent genetic alterations observed in ovarian cancer. In contrast to conventional markers such as CA125, circulating tumor DNA (ctDNA) provides information about tumor mutations and insights into treatment response. Analysis of ctDNA enables the identification of tumor-associated mutations. Non-coding RNAs (ncRNAs) also influence cellular processes and act as effectors in oncogenic pathways by binding to RNA or proteins. One effector is Metastasis-Associated Lung Adenocarcinoma Transcript 1 (MALAT1), whose increased expression is associated with an aggressive tumor phenotype. MicroRNAs (miRNAs) are crucial in regulating the expression of genes associated with ovarian cancer development and progression. Exosomes carrying various molecules, including miRNAs and lncRNAs, contribute to ovarian cancer progression. Adipocytokines play an important role in the regulation of metabolic and inflammatory processes. Despite their diagnostic potential, the identified biomarkers require further validation.

title: Testicular and Rumen Microbial Responses to Selenium-Enriched Malt in Heat-Exposed Simmental Bulls.
abstract: This study evaluated testicular and rumen microbial responses to selenium-enriched malt in heat-exposed Simmental bulls. Eighteen bulls received a basal diet alone or supplemented to provide target supplemental Se levels of 0.3 or 0.5 mg/kg dietary DM. Metagenomics included six bulls per group, host assays four per group, and RNA sequencing three per group. Compared with controls, the high-dose group had higher serum antioxidant indices and reproductive hormone concentrations, lower inflammatory markers, higher Johnsen scores, and lower TUNEL positivity. Gene-level FDR control identified 23, 1, and 4 differentially expressed genes in the low-dose versus control, high-dose versus control, and high-dose versus low-dose contrasts, respectively. Provider-reported GSEA showed negative normalized enrichment scores for steroid biosynthesis in the control-versus-low-dose and control-versus-high-dose contrasts, indicating enrichment toward the supplemented side under the provider's contrast convention. qPCR showed lower CYP11A1, CYP17A1, SCARB1, and LDLR expression at the low dose, whereas Bax, Bcl-2, and CYP17A1 protein abundance did not differ. Rumen microbial diversity and community composition differed among groups, and two post hoc selected cofactor-related pathways had lower abundance at the low dose. None of the 160 microbiome-testis or 720 microbiome-serum associations survived FDR correction. Supplementation was associated with favorable systemic and testicular histological responses and dose-specific molecular and microbial changes under heat exposure.

title: RNA Modification Profiles and m6A Regulatory Patterns in the Lungs of Sheep at Different Altitudes.
abstract: The lung is a key organ for oxygen uptake and gas exchange and plays an important role in adaptation to hypoxic environments at high altitudes. RNA modifications represent an important layer of epitranscriptomic regulation and participate in cellular processes by affecting RNA stability, splicing, translation, and degradation. In this study, the right lung parenchyma from low-altitude Hu sheep (LL), mid-altitude Tibetan sheep (ML), and high-altitude Tibetan sheep (HL) were used to investigate altitude-associated RNA modification profiles and m6A regulatory patterns. A UPLC-MS/MS platform was employed to quantitatively detect 55 RNA modifications, while RT-qPCR and Western blot analyses were performed to evaluate the expression of HIF1α, HIF2α, and m6A-related regulatory factors. The results showed distinct differences in lung RNA modification profiles among the three groups. Compared with the LL and ML groups, the HL group exhibited reduced m6A and m6Am levels, whereas several non- m6A modifications, including t6A, m1G, m2G, m7G, m3C, and m5C, showed increasing trends. The expression levels of HIF1α and HIF2α were higher in the ML and HL groups than in the LL group. In addition, METTL3, METTL14, WTAP, and several YTH family reader proteins were downregulated in the HL group at both the protein and mRNA levels. These findings indicate that sheep lung RNA modification profiles and the m6A regulatory machinery differ among groups with different altitude-related adaptation backgrounds. Collectively, these findings reveal epitranscriptomic differences associated with altitude and breed in sheep lungs and provide a basis for further investigation of the role of m6A regulation in high-altitude adaptation.

title: LncRNA-Mediated Regulation of Hepatic Metabolic Homeostasis: Cholesterol, Triglyceride, Glucose and Pathological Implications.
abstract: The liver coordinately maintains cholesterol, triglyceride, and glucose homeostasis by integrating the synthesis, storage, utilization, and inter-conversion of these metabolic programs, and their dysregulation contributes to metabolic-associated steatotic liver disease (MASLD), hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC), type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2DM), and gestational diabetes mellitus (GDM). Long non-coding RNAs (lncRNAs), which are not translated into proteins, regulate gene expression through interactions with DNA, RNA, and proteins at transcriptional, post-transcriptional, and epigenetic levels, and have emerged as central determinants of hepatic metabolic balance. This review systematically summarizes how lncRNAs govern cholesterol biosynthesis and efflux, triglyceride synthesis and lipolysis, glycogen turnover, gluconeogenesis, and glycolysis in hepatocytes. Unlike pathway-by-pathway descriptions, we highlight that these programs are coupled through shared signaling networks, including PI3K/AKT/mechanistic target of rapamycin complex 1 (mTORC1), 5'-AMP-activated protein kinase (AMPK), SREBP, PPAR, and FoxO1, and that pleiotropic lncRNAs coordinate lipid and glucose outputs rather than controlling a single isolated process. We further examine how lncRNA dysregulation drives MASLD, HCC, T2DM, and GDM, and evaluate their potential as diagnostic biomarkers and therapeutic targets. Finally, we outline current limitations, including incomplete molecular characterization, low cross-species conservation, heterogeneous experimental validation, and unresolved delivery challenges, which must be addressed before lncRNA-based strategies reach clinical application.

title: Prey Preference of the Freshwater Jellyfish Craspedacusta sowerbii: Integrated Behavioral Observations and Transcriptomic Responses to Phytoplankton and Zooplankton.
abstract: Freshwater ecosystems are highly vulnerable to biological invasions. The globally distributed invasive hydrozoan Craspedacusta sowerbii imposes strong top-down pressure on plankton communities owing to its distinct feeding selectivity. While prior studies have confirmed its preferential predation on zooplankton over phytoplankton, the integrated mechanisms underlying this prey discrimination remain poorly understood. Here, we integrated behavioral observations and comparative transcriptomics to investigate the prey preference strategy of adult C. sowerbii medusae. Behavioral assays demonstrated active predation exclusively on zooplankton, with no targeted hunting toward phytoplankton. Microscopic observations revealed efficient degradation of ingested zooplankton within 6 h, whereas phytoplankton cells were excreted with no apparent digestion. Transcriptomic analyses indicated that zooplankton feeding induces profound transcriptional reprogramming in C. sowerbii. Genes related to catalytic and hydrolase activities were significantly enriched, accompanied by substantial up-regulation of ribosome biogenesis and mitochondrial oxidative phosphorylation. In contrast, phytoplankton exposure triggered negligible metabolic perturbation. The coordinated activation of hydrolase, protein synthesis, energy metabolism, cytoskeletal movement, and mucus production forms the potential physiological basis for the feeding preference of C. sowerbii. Field observations further suggest that algicidal bacteria in the gastric cavity of medusae may assist auxiliary phytoplankton utilization. This study elucidates the regulatory mechanisms governing the trophic selectivity of C. sowerbii, fills key knowledge gaps in its feeding ecology, and offers new insights into the environmental adaptability and survival strategies of this species.

title: BmS6K Regulates Growth and Survival Traits of Silkworm, Bombyx mori.
abstract: Ribosomal protein S6 kinase (S6K) is a conserved effector of the mTOR signaling pathway that regulates cell growth and metabolism. The organism-level function of S6K in the silkworm Bombyx mori has not yet been examined by direct genetic manipulation. Here, we combined CRISPR/Cas9-mediated knockout, piggyBac-based transgenic re-expression and overexpression, and multi-tissue RNA-seq with weighted gene co-expression network analysis (WGCNA) to characterize the role of BmS6K in vivo. BmS6K-null mutants were viable but showed 26.5% and 28.6% reductions in pupal weight in males and females, respectively. Furthermore, mutant survival rates were 44.2% (males) and 28.5% (females) lower than those of controls, with mortality concentrated at the late fifth larval stage. Targeted transgenic re-expression rescued these phenotypic defects. Conversely, overexpressing BmS6K in a wild-type background increased the larval growth rate by 16.9% and significantly raised both whole cocoon weight and pupal weights. WGCNA of the three tissue types identified a core co-expression module (MEred) that was significantly enriched for genes involved in proton-transporting V-type ATPase activity and vacuolar complex assembly, mTOR signaling, and oxidative phosphorylation coupled to cellular redox homeostasis, including BmV1-ATPase, BmGabaT, and BmNadDac, whose orthologs represent core components or mediate critical cross-talk in the TOR-S6K pathway, a function conserved in Drosophila and mammals. Since the loss and gain of BmS6K produced opposite effects on growth and viability, it can be regarded as a candidate target for increasing cocoon yield in sericulture, as well as a target for RNAi-based control of lepidopteran pests through the suppression of its orthologs.

title: PTBP1: A Key Hub and a Potential Therapeutic Target in High-Grade Glioma.
abstract: High-grade gliomas (HGGs) are lethal primary brain tumors with poor prognosis despite multimodal therapy. Polypyrimidine tract-binding protein 1 (PTBP1) is an RNA-binding protein that regulates alternative splicing, mRNA stability, and translation. In HGGs, PTBP1 is overexpressed and correlates with tumor grade, IDH mutation status, and patient survival, supporting it as a candidate prognostic biomarker and therapeutic target. Structurally, PTBP1 contains four RNA recognition motifs connected by flexible linkers, conferring conformational plasticity for diverse RNA interactions. In glioma cells, upstream regulators-including non-coding RNAs and post-translational modifications-dysregulate PTBP1, converting it from a physiological regulator into a predominantly oncogenic driver. Multiple lines of evidence suggest that PTBP1 drives malignancy through three interconnected mechanisms: oncogenic splicing switching, stabilization of oncogenic mRNAs, and IRES-dependent translation. Although no selective, direct small-molecule inhibitor of PTBP1 has yet been clinically validated, repurposed compounds (e.g., venetoclax) and indirect modulators have shown preliminary antitumor activity in preclinical models. However, direct target engagement, in vivo efficacy, and blood-brain barrier penetration remain insufficiently established. This review summarizes PTBP1's structure, upstream networks, downstream mechanisms, and therapeutic potential, highlighting the need for further validation of PTBP1-centered strategies prior to clinical translation.

title: The m6A Reader IGF2BP2 Drives Depressive-like Behaviors Through m6A-Dependent Repression of Astrocytic GLUT1 and Glucose Metabolism.
abstract: Major depressive disorder (MDD) is a severe psychiatric condition with complex etiology and limited therapeutic targets. In this study, we identify the m6A reader protein IGF2BP2 as a critical epigenetic regulator in depression. We demonstrate that IGF2BP2 expression is significantly upregulated in the hippocampus of both MDD patients and mice subjected to chronic unpredictable mild stress (CUMS). Further, hippocampal knockdown of Igf2bp2 ameliorated depressive-like behaviors in mice. Mechanistically, we demonstrated that the IGF2BP2 protein, specifically in astrocytes, binds to the mRNA of glucose transporter 1 (GLUT1) and regulates the expression of GLUT1 in an m6A-dependent manner, mainly by promoting its decay, leading to impaired astrocytic glucose uptake. Moreover, overexpression of Glut1 rescued both glucose metabolic deficits and depressive-like behaviors. Taken together, our findings reveal a previously unrecognized IGF2BP2-GLUT1 axis in the pathogenesis of depression and highlight its potential as a therapeutic target for antidepressant intervention.

title: Rapid FAK Phosphorylation and Progressive Tight-Junction Protein Alterations Under Hyperosmotic Stress in Corneal Epithelial Cells.
abstract: Dry eye disease (DED) is characterized by tear hyperosmolality and ocular surface injury, but the contribution of focal adhesion kinase (FAK)-related signaling to tight junction (TJ) protein alterations remains unclear. We combined a scopolamine hydrobromide (SCOP)-induced desiccating stress mouse model with human corneal epithelial (HCE-T) cells exposed to NaCl-induced hyperosmolarity, together with transcriptomics, immunofluorescence, immunoblotting, pharmacological inhibition, and siRNA-mediated FAK knockdown. RNA sequencing identified 823 significant large-effect differentially expressed genes; analysis of the 3741 FDR-corrected significant genes revealed significant enrichment of focal adhesion, extracellular matrix-receptor, cell adhesion, and tight junction pathways. In HCE-T cells, hyperosmotic stress increased FAK Tyr397 phosphorylation as early as 1 h without changing total FAK. At 24 h, p-FAK declined while total FAK protein levels remained stable, consistent with dephosphorylation at Tyr397; by 48 h, total FAK protein was lost, accompanied by cell injury. TJ protein abundance and junctional continuity decreased progressively with increasing osmolarity and exposure duration. PF-562271, a dual FAK/Pyk2 inhibitor, produced a concentration-dependent reduction in FAK Tyr397 phosphorylation and, at 2.5 μM, also reduced Pyk2 Tyr402 phosphorylation while partially preserving ZO-1, claudin-1, and occludin abundance. FAK knockdown independently attenuated TJ protein loss and partially preserved ZO-1 junctional continuity under 500 mOsm/L hyperosmotic stress. These findings support a time-dependent contribution of FAK-related signaling to hyperosmotic stress-induced TJ protein remodeling.

title: HOXA5 Targets ABCD1 and IRF7 to Regulate the Proliferation and Differentiation of Goat Intramuscular Preadipocytes.
abstract: Intramuscular fat (IMF) is crucial for goat meat quality, being influenced by preadipocyte proliferation and differentiation. Although the developmental transcription factor HOXA5 is associated with adipose tissue development and lipid deposition in mice, its role in goat adipogenesis remains unclear. This study investigated HOXA5's role in regulating IMF lipid deposition in goats. Regarding differentiation, HOXA5 overexpression reduced mRNA and protein levels of differentiation genes, including CEBP/α and CEBP/β. Additionally, Oil Red O and Bodipy staining demonstrated a decrease in lipid accumulation in the HOXA5 overexpression group. Conversely, these phenotypes showed opposite trends in the HOXA5 knockdown group. Regarding proliferation, HOXA5 overexpression upregulated mRNA levels of proliferation genes, enhanced cell vitality, and increased the proportion of EdU-positive cells, while HOXA5 knockdown inhibited these phenotypes. Mechanistically, IRF7 and ABCD1 were identified as the target genes of HOXA5 by RNA-Seq and dual luciferase reporter gene assay. Functional analyses further showed that IRF7 promoted both proliferation and adipogenic differentiation, whereas ABCD1 inhibited both processes. Rescue experiments supported the involvement of IRF7 and ABCD1 in HOXA5-induced promotion of proliferation and inhibition of adipogenic differentiation. These results highlight HOXA5's critical regulatory role in goat intramuscular adipocyte lipid deposition, offering novel insights into the underlying molecular mechanisms.

title: Effects of Combined Basal and Bud-Stage Foliar KH2PO4 Application on Vegetative Growth, Floral Performance and Nutrient Partitioning in Potted Hydrangea paniculata 'Limelight'.
abstract: Phosphorus (P) and potassium (K) are essential mineral nutrients for plant growth, development, and reproduction, and their supply levels and application methods may affect the growth, physiological performance, and flowering quality of ornamental plants. In this study, one-year-old potted cuttings of Hydrangea paniculata 'Limelight' were used in a two-factor completely randomized design. Four basal application rates of KH2PO4 (50, 100, 150, and 200 mg P2O5 kg-1 substrate) were combined with foliar application of 0.1% KH2PO4 at the bud stage. Root morphology, biomass allocation, photosynthetic characteristics, antioxidant physiology, flowering quality, and the accumulation and allocation of N, P, and K among plant organs were evaluated. Transcriptome sequencing and quantitative reverse transcription PCR (qRT-PCR) validation were also performed for representative treatments. The results showed that treatment 2KF, which combined basal application of 100 mg P2O5 kg-1 substrate with foliar application at the bud stage, exhibited a favorable balance between physiological performance and flowering traits. The maximum quantum efficiency of PSII (Fv/Fm) in leaves was 0.76, significantly higher than that in treatments 1KF and 4KF. The leaf soluble sugar content reached 13.12 mg g-1 fresh weight (FW), whereas the malondialdehyde (MDA) content remained relatively low. The root-to-shoot ratio was 1.56 ± 0.48, 38.1% higher than that of the control (CK) and higher than those of the other treatments. Transcriptome analysis identified 8142 differentially expressed genes (DEGs) between 2KF and the nitrogen-only control (CN), including 3386 upregulated and 4756 downregulated genes. These DEGs were primarily associated with nutrient transport, photosynthesis, carbon metabolism, antioxidant responses, and stress responses. In treatment 2KF, the expression of several genes associated with P and K transport was upregulated, whereas the expression of genes related to the phosphate starvation response was suppressed. The expression patterns of 12 candidate genes examined by qRT-PCR were generally consistent with the RNA-seq results. In conclusion, under the conditions of this experiment, basal KH2PO4 application combined with foliar application at the bud stage, particularly treatment 2KF, produced favorable overall responses in Hydrangea paniculata 'Limelight'. These findings provide a reference for optimizing fertilization management in this ornamental cultivar.

title: Cadmium Dose-Responsive Transcriptomics Prioritizes CvHMA15 and CvHMA16 in Cardamine violifolia.
abstract: Cadmium (Cd) responses in metal-accumulating plants involve coordinated stress programs and specialized metal transporters, but the relationship between these levels remains poorly resolved in Cardamine violifolia. Here, seeds were germinated for seven days under 0, 10, 25, or 100 mg L-1 CdCl2, followed by root phenotyping and dose-resolved transcriptome analysis. Root growth showed a biphasic pattern: root length increased at 10 mg L-1, whereas growth at 100 mg L-1 was strongly reduced relative to the low-dose treatment. RNA-seq of 12 libraries identified 5665 genes that responded in at least one comparison and resolved six expression trajectories. Pathway analysis indicated low-dose metabolic adjustment, strong activation of phenylpropanoid, signaling, and xenobiotic-response pathways at 25 mg L-1, and broader transcriptional repression at 100 mg L-1. Cross-referencing the transcriptome with 16 reference-identified CvHMA loci prioritized CvHMA15 and CvHMA16 as a 99.87 identical protein pair with divergent regulation: CvHMA15 was moderately down-regulated across the Cd gradient, whereas CvHMA16 was induced and met the combined differential-expression threshold at 100 mg L-1. In a pYES2.0-based yeast spot assay, expression of either CvHMA15 or CvHMA16 maintained colony growth across five cell densities on medium containing 50 μM CdCl2, whereas the empty-vector control was strongly inhibited; growth was comparable among transformants in the absence of Cd. These results establish a transcriptome-guided framework for candidate prioritization while leaving transport direction and in planta mechanism to direct functional tests.

title: Transcriptome-Informed Digital Twins Reveal a Functional Response Landscape in Prostate Cancer.
abstract: Prostate cancer (PCa) shows substantial inter-sample molecular heterogeneity, yet static molecular profiles provide limited information about how individual tumours respond to changes in signalling activity. We developed a transcriptome-informed digital-twin framework that translates tumour-specific molecular states into simulated functional responses. RNA-sequencing data from 492 primary TCGA-PRAD tumour samples were scored across 1628 Reactome pathways. Of these, 220 unique pathways (232 pathway-to-node assignments) were selected through biologically informed mapping and aggregated into eight functional nodes used to personalise individual digital twins (DTs). Each DT was simulated under six conditions: baseline and five perturbations involving AR (androgen receptor) suppression, PI3K/AKT suppression, TGF-β induction, combined AR and PI3K/AKT suppression, and combined AR suppression with TGF-β induction. These simulations produced a 42-feature behavioural fingerprint for each tumour. PCA identified a continuous functional response space, with the first three components accounting for 80.75% of behavioural variance. The dominant response axis was associated with Gleason score (Spearman ρ=0.30, FDR-adjusted p<0.001), while TP53 mutation status was associated with PC1 and PC3 after multiple-testing correction. Responses to individual perturbations varied between tumour samples and were coordinated across pathway interventions. Combined perturbations were largely additive, with relative deviations below 3% across the principal functional outputs. The dominant simulation-derived axis closely corresponded to the major static transcriptomic axis, indicating that the model primarily re-expressed, rather than replaced, the underlying molecular structure. The major variance structure was preserved across personalisation strengths, whereas discrete HDBSCAN solutions depended on the parameter setting. Ablation analysis showed that transcriptome-informed parameter personalisation was necessary to preserve inter-sample differences in baseline steady states. Overall, the results describe PCa heterogeneity as a continuous functional response space and position transcriptome-informed DTs as a mechanistic re-expression of molecular profiles that enables explicit, hypothesis-generating counterfactual perturbation analyses.

title: Luteolin and Naringenin from Herbal Medicines Suppress Pulmonary Arterial Smooth Muscle Cell Hyperproliferation in Pulmonary Arterial Hypertension by Modulating IGF1R/PI3K/AKT Signaling.
abstract: Pulmonary arterial hypertension (PAH) remains a progressive disease with limited therapies. As part of our continuing study to identify effective agents for PAH from natural herbal medicines, we analyzed the chemical constituents of an empirically validated herbal formula named Guilou Tongluo formula (GLTL) by UHPLC-Q-Exactive MS, retrieved its putative blood-absorbed constituents from databases, and integrated them with lung RNA-sequencing data to discover potential active constituents against PAH. A compound-disease network was constructed; drug-disease intersection genes underwent functional enrichment analysis, whereas hub targets were prioritized by protein-protein interaction analysis. Immune infiltration and single-cell RNA sequencing were used to analyze the vascular microenvironment, while nomogram and decision curve analyses exploratorily assessed the association of candidate targets with disease status at the tissue level. Target engagement was predicted by molecular docking and molecular dynamics simulation and supported by cellular thermal shift and drug affinity target stability assays; the mechanism of the constituents was then examined. The results showed that GLTL attenuated proliferation and promoted apoptosis in PDGF-BB-stimulated pulmonary arterial smooth muscle cells (PASMCs), an effect associated with IGF1R/PI3K/AKT signaling in smooth muscle cells, with IGF1R identified as a key candidate target. Molecular docking and dynamics simulation predicted that naringenin and luteolin could bind IGF1R, and CETSA and DARTS provided experimental support for IGF1R engagement. Both compounds engaged IGF1R and suppressed IGF-1/IGF1R signaling, thereby reducing PI3K/AKT phosphorylation and the expression of Cyclin D1, BCL2, PCNA, and Ki67. In summary, luteolin and naringenin are potential active constituents of GLTL that suppress proliferation and promote apoptosis in PDGF-BB-stimulated PASMCs in vitro, an effect associated with suppression of IGF1R/PI3K/AKT signaling.

title: miR-195-5p Reduces VEGFA Expression and Angiogenesis in Colorectal Cancer.
abstract: Angiogenesis is a key process in colorectal cancer (CRC) progression, with vascular endothelial growth factor A (VEGFA) being a major pro-angiogenic mediator. miR-195-5p has previously been identified by our group as a tumor-suppressive miRNA downregulated in CRC. Here, we aimed to investigate whether miR-195-5p contributes to CRC-associated angiogenenic processes through VEGFA regulation. Potential miR-195-5p targets were investigated through bioinformatic predictions and miRNA Target RNA immunoprecipitation. VEGFA expression was evaluated in public CRC datasets and paired tumor/adjacent tissues of a cohort of CRC patients by quantitative real-time PCR and immunohistochemistry. miR-195-5p gain- and loss-of-function experiments were performed in CRC cells to assess VEGFA and VEGFR2 expression and extracellular VEGF-A levels by ELISA. Endothelial tube formation assays using HUVECs were conducted to evaluate paracrine angiogenic effects. VEGFA expression was also analyzed in an AOM/DSS-induced murine CRC model treated with a miR-195-5p mimic. VEGFA was predicted as a conserved miR-195-5p target and was enriched in miR-195-5p-associated RISCs. VEGFA was overexpressed in CRC tissues compared to normal or adjacent non-tumor tissues. miR-195-5p restoration reduced VEGFA mRNA and protein expression, extracellular VEGF-A levels, and VEGFR2 protein levels in the HCT116 CRC cell line, whereas miR-195-5p inhibition produced the opposite molecular profile. Conditioned media from miR-195-5p-overexpressing CRC cells significantly impaired endothelial tube formation. Consistently, miR-195-5p in vivo administration reduced colonic Vegfa expression in AOM/DSS-treated mice. Overall, these findings indicate that miR-195-5p negatively modulates VEGFA expression and reduces the ability of CRC cell-derived conditioned media to support endothelial tube formation. This study extends the tumor-suppressive functions previously attributed to miR-195-5p by supporting its involvement in the regulation of angiogenesis-related processes in CRC.

title: Genome-Wide Characterization and Multidimensional Transcriptome Profiling of the SABATH Methyltransferase Gene Family in Sunflower (Helianthus annuus L.).
abstract: Plant SABATH methyltransferases contribute to volatile formation, hormone homeostasis and stress responses, but their family-wide organization in sunflower remains poorly characterized. Using the HanXRQr2.0-SUNRISE reference genome, we identified 33 high-confidence HaSABATH genes and integrated phylogenetic, duplication, synteny, promoter and protein-structure analyses with expression profiles from 200 public RNA sequencing (RNA-seq) libraries representing 87 distinct conditions. Twelve genes belonged to the salicylic acid/jasmonic acid methyltransferase-related Clade I, 19 to the benzoic acid/salicylic acid methyltransferase-related Clade II, and two to other lineages. Tandem, proximal, dispersed and whole-genome/segmental duplication contributed to the family, with overlapping tandem and segmental evidence for HaSABATH4 and HaSABATH15. Eleven reliable nonsynonymous-to-synonymous substitution ratios were below one. Most predicted proteins showed high model confidence. Across the sampled conditions, Clade I members generally showed higher expression levels and broader expression, while many Clade II members were weakly expressed or condition-biased. HaSABATH4 and HaSABATH6 were prioritized for follow-up under combined saline-alkali stress. This integrated analysis links evolutionary context to expression divergence and provides candidates for targeted biochemical and genetic studies.

title: The WNT Inhibitor PRI-724 Depletes Endogenous SOX2 and Blocks SOX2 Upregulation by Therapeutic Regimes.
abstract: Background/Objectives: The stem cell transcription factor SOX2 is expressed in more than 20 types of cancer. SOX2 expression is also elevated by a wide range of clinically used drugs and has been linked causally to drug and radiation resistance. Hence, SOX2 is recognized as an important therapeutic target. This study set out to identify a small molecule inhibitor that reduces SOX2 in a wide range of tumor types. Methods: In this study, the WNT inhibitor, PRI-724 (Foscenvivint), was tested for its ability to downregulate SOX2 in ten tumor cell lines using western blot analysis. We also used western blot analysis to examine whether PRI-724 blocks the upregulation of SOX2 by clinically used drugs and radiation. Additionally, we examined the overall effects of PRI-724 on the transcriptome by performing RNA-Seq and STRING analysis. Results: PRI-724 not only downregulated SOX2 in ten different tumor cell lines representing eight different tumor types, but also blocked the upregulation of SOX2 induced by vemurafenib, gemcitabine and radiation. Besides downregulating SOX2 at the protein and RNA level, without altering the stability of SOX2 RNA, PRI-724 significantly modified the transcriptome. STRING analysis of the upregulated and downregulated genes indicates that PRI-724 altered the expression of genes involved in stress-response pathways, including endoplasmic reticulum (ER) stress. Conclusions: The WNT inhibitor PRI-724 downregulates SOX2 expression in a wide range of tumor cell types and blocks the upregulation of SOX2 by clinically used regimens. PRI-724 also modulates the expression of genes associated with stress-response pathways.

title: Cortical thinning and functional reorganization as well as related transcriptomic signatures during early motor recovery following acute basal ganglia ischemic stroke.
abstract: Acute basal ganglia ischemic stroke (ABGIS) commonly causes severe motor impairment, yet early spatiotemporal patterns of cortical morphological alterations and functional reorganization alongside the spatially coupled transcriptomic signatures remain unclear. Twenty-six ABGIS patients and thirty-three normal controls (NCs) received multimodal MRI and neurological examinations, and patients were reassessed at 1-month follow-up. Cortical morphological changes and brain functional reorganization were analyzed based on cortical thickness (CT) and functional connectivity (FC). We identified the most discriminative FC features based on machine learning (ML) classification and interpretability analyses, and investigated transcriptomic signatures associated with FC alterations via the Allen Human Brain Atlas. No differences in CT were found between baseline ABGIS patients (ABGIS_1) and NCs. Compared with ABGIS_1, follow-up patients (ABGIS_2) exhibited reduced CT in the left postcentral gyrus (PoCG.L), left superior parietal lobule (SPL.L), and left supramarginal gyrus (SMG.L). Compared with NCs, ABGIS_1 showed decreased FC from PoCG.L/SPL.L to sensorimotor cortex and occipital cortex. ABGIS_2 presented elevated FC relative to ABGIS_1 between PoCG.L and the right precentral gyrus (PreCG.R), and between SPL.L and the bilateral precentral gyrus as well as right superior occipital gyrus. Longitudinal increases in FC between PoCG.L/SPL.L and PreCG.R were positively correlated with improvements in Fugl-Meyer Assessment scores. ML models coupled with interpretability analyses preliminarily demonstrated that FC between PoCG.L/SPL.L and PreCG.R made prominent contributions to classification. Transcriptomic analysis revealed that gene sets correlated with FC alterations were mainly enriched in neuronal synaptic structure and synaptic signaling, chromatin regulation, as well as DNA and RNA metabolism. This study verifies progressive cortical thinning and adaptive functional reorganization during early motor recovery following ABGIS, with such brain functional alterations paralleling distinct transcriptomic signatures, providing neuropathological and spatial transcriptomic clues for interpreting early motor recovery.

title: Concordant Metabolite Differences Across Cecal Content, Liver, and Plasma in Mice Fed an Obesogenic Diet Containing Common Bean (Phaseolus vulgaris L.): A Multi-Compartment Metabolomics Study.
abstract: Background/Objectives: How metabolic changes accompanying common bean (Phaseolus vulgaris L.) consumption are organized across gut, liver, and blood, and which are separable from lower adiposity, is unclear. Methods: Male C57BL/6J mice were fed an obesogenic diet with or without cooked bean powder supplying 70% (nominal) of total dietary protein for 14 weeks; diets were assigned to whole cages (4 per diet). Diets were formulated to nominally match macronutrient proportions (w/w) from ingredient and supplier values; sources, and hence estimated protein, amino acid, α-linolenate, and fiber supply, differed; intake was not measured. Cecal content, liver, and plasma were profiled by untargeted metabolomics and liver by RNA-seq for selected gene sets. Metabolite classes selected by three-compartment concordance were examined against prior predictions. Results: Diet groups separated in every compartment, most strongly in cecal content. In all three, 36 host metabolites differed concordantly and 22 KEGG pathways were significant. Five classes met the selection criteria: branched-chain amino acids and their keto acids accumulated in cecal content despite lower estimated supply; long-chain n-3 and n-6 fatty acids shifted reciprocally while hepatic Fads2, Elovl5, and Fads1 transcripts were 45-61% of control; and glutathione-related metabolites, ceramides, and bile acids differed as predicted. Total depot mass was significantly lower only in the full cohort (-12%). After MANCOVA adjustment for depot redistribution and hepatic lipid, the branched-chain class retained its diet association (q-value = 0.012), the glutathione-related (q-value = 0.047) and n-3 (q-value = 0.049) classes did so provisionally, the former and the hepatic component of the latter depending on one cage in cage-aware models, and ceramides (q-value = 0.20) and bile acids (q-value = 0.15) did not. Conclusions: Whether these differences drive or follow the leaner phenotype requires time-course, single-constituent designs in both sexes.

title: Protein Biomarkers of Kidney Injury and Dysfunction: Emerging Evidence on Non-Coding RNAs.
abstract: Background: Kidney biomarkers address different clinical questions, and their accuracy depends on the population, sample, timing, and outcome. Objective: To organize selected evidence on protein biomarkers of kidney injury and dysfunction and examine emerging clinical evidence on non-coding RNAs (ncRNAs). Methods: This structured comparative narrative review used PubMed and Google Scholar, with searches through 19 September 2026, supplemented by targeted source verification and literature updating during revision in October 2026. Published estimates were summarized descriptively, no new meta-analysis was performed. Filtration assessment, AKI detection, persistence, disease activity, and RNA discovery or validation were considered separately. Results: Cystatin C and proenkephalin provide filtration-related information; KIM-1, NGAL, L-FABP, and NAG address tubular injury or associated outcomes. Urinary IL-18 and serum IL-8 have limited stand-alone diagnostic value in pediatric AKI. [TIMP-2]×[IGFBP7] reflects cellular stress and near-term AKI risk. CCL14 concerns persistent AKI. uDKK3, VCAM-1, and serum cathepsin S have evidence specific to their applications. Urinary HBP and plasma 8-isoprostane describe complementary infection and oxidative-stress contexts. More recent syntheses revise previously reported estimates for KIM-1 and NGAL. Selected ncRNA studies show promising discrimination, but their populations, clinical contrasts, and validation stages differ. Conclusions: Organizing biomarkers by clinical question connects their biological information with distinct diagnostic and prognostic applications. Protein-ncRNA combinations offer a direction for prospective research, with clinical adoption requiring independent validation and added value beyond conventional assessment.

title: Endogenous Retrovirus-Targeted Immunotherapy for Non-Small Cell Lung Cancer Supported by Cellular HERV-K Expression, Dependency and Efficacy of ERV Therapy in a Murine Model.
abstract: Human endogenous retrovirus-K (HERV-K/HML-2) has been associated with non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC), but its functional relevance and the potential for HERV-directed immunotherapy remains unresolved. Here, we characterized HERV-K expression across 207 advanced NSCLC patient biopsies by total RNA-seq observing widespread expression of HERV-K Gag and Env antigen encoding sequences. The Env-ORF that disrupted HERV-K102 was strongly associated with interferon and antigen-presenting programs, identifying it as a marker of an immune-activated tumor state. shRNA-mediated knockdown of HERV-K in five NSCLC cell lines with distinct driver mutations impaired proliferation and survival. In separate experiments, exposure of these cell lines to treatment-related stressors, including cytokines (TNF-α and IFN-γ) and chemotherapy, revealed dynamic patterns of HERV-K protein accumulation with antigen expression retained, and in some cases increased. Immunotherapeutic targeting was performed using the ASB-XIV mouse NSCLC cell line and a murine ERV surrogate antigen using adenovirus to express murine leukemia virus (MLV) antigen on a mouse β-retroviral particle structurally related to HERV-K. This immunization was able to elicit significant protection against tumor challenge and additive benefit with anti-PD-L1 in therapeutic treatment, establishing proof-of-concept for ERV-targeted immunotherapy in a murine surrogate system rather than direct evidence of HERV-K-targeted efficacy. Our findings suggest an important role of HERV-K in NSCLC immunobiology and that adaptive immunity targeting HERV-K should be explored in the treatment of NSCLC patients.

title: Integrated Transcriptomic and Proteomic Analyses Reveal Molecular and Cellular Responses to INHA Manipulation in Primary Yak Sertoli Cells.
abstract: INHA encodes the α-subunit of inhibin A and inhibin B and is involved in the regulation of male reproductive endocrinology; however, its cellular function in yak Sertoli cells remains poorly understood. In this study, primary yak Sertoli cells from 3-month-old donors were used to establish INHA overexpression and knockdown models, followed by RNA sequencing (RNA-Seq), directDIA quantitative proteomics, integrated transcriptome-proteome analysis, and functional assays. Donor-aware, false discovery rate (FDR)-controlled analyses identified 949 differentially expressed genes (DEGs) and 1388 differentially abundant proteins (DAPs) following overexpression, and 28 DEGs and 54 DAPs following knockdown. The two manipulations produced non-equivalent molecular responses under their respective experimental conditions. Functional enrichment analyses highlighted cytokine-related signaling, DNA replication and cell-cycle regulation, energy metabolism, and cell-matrix-related responses. TNF signaling was significantly enriched at both omics levels, whereas NF-κB signaling was significantly enriched at the transcriptomic level. Integrated analysis identified 98 molecules altered at both the mRNA and protein levels after INHA overexpression, of which 96 showed concordant changes. CCL2, CCL5, IL1RL1, LIF, CTSC, HK2, FN1, and ITGA11 were prioritized as representative INHA-responsive candidates, while quantitative reverse transcription PCR (qRT-PCR) supported selected transcript-level changes. Flow cytometry showed that INHA overexpression was associated with increased apoptosis and a lower proportion of viable cells, whereas knockdown produced the opposite pattern. β-Tubulin immunofluorescence revealed qualitative differences in microtubule staining patterns. These results characterize molecular and cellular responses associated with INHA perturbation and prioritize candidate pathways and molecules for further investigation in yak Sertoli cells.

title: Reproducible Interferon-Centered Microglial Response at 7 Days After Traumatic Brain Injury: A Transcriptomic Meta-Analysis with Focus on the BTK/NOX2 Panel.
abstract: Traumatic brain injury (TBI) drives sustained microglial activation and secondary neurodegeneration. The Bruton's tyrosine kinase (BTK)-NADPH oxidase 2 (NOX2) axis has been proposed as a convergent node, but transcriptional evidence has largely been derived from individual studies. Our primary aim was to characterize the microglial response at 7 days post-injury, and our secondary aim was to evaluate BTK/NOX2-associated genes within this response. We performed a random-effects meta-analysis (metafor, REML) of four independent mouse microglial RNA-seq datasets (16,636 genes). Differential expression estimates were pooled across datasets and characterized by protein-protein interaction network analysis, functional enrichment (GO, Reactome, KEGG), weighted gene co-expression analysis, and gene set enrichment analysis. A curated 14-gene BTK/NOX2 panel was tested at the individual-gene and aggregate levels. The meta-analysis identified 160 significant genes at 7 days (117 upregulated, 43 downregulated). Interferon signaling was the most consistent program, supported by gene set enrichment, over-representation analysis, and the largest network cluster. It comprised antigen presentation, a lipid-handling signature resembling disease-associated microglia (Lpl, log2FC = 3.86), and partially reduced homeostatic genes. Within the panel, Cybb was the only significant gene (log2FC = 1.66, adjusted p = 0.019) that increased in the same direction in all four datasets, whereas no significant change was detected at the panel level, although statistical power was limited by the small number of genes (n = 14). The 7-day microglial response is interferon-centered and reproducible, and the BTK/NOX2 signal is limited to a transcript-level increase in Cybb.

title: Exploring the landscape of clinical research in AATD: a cross-sectional review of registered studies in clinicaltrials.gov, clinicaltrialsregister.eu, and WHO ICTRP.
abstract: Since the approval of human alpha-1 proteinase inhibitor in 1987 for treating alpha-1 antitrypsin deficiency (AATD)-related emphysema, no new targeted therapies have been authorized for this condition. Notably, effective treatments addressing the extrapulmonary manifestations of AATD remain lacking. This review provides a comprehensive overview of the current landscape and progress in clinical development for AATD therapies. A comprehensive search of all registered trials was performed on 26 March 2025 across the web-based databases of ClinicalTrials.gov, Clinical Trials Register Europe, and the World Health Organization International Clinical Trials Registry Platform. A total of 147 studies were identified. Of these, 112 (76.2%) were interventional studies and 35 (23.8%) were observational studies. The median actual enrollment in interventional studies was 33 participants, compared with a median planned enrollment of 55 participants. The pharmaceutical industry (57%) was the main source of financial support for these studies. The most prominent study locations were North America (51.7%) and Europe (42.9%), followed by Oceania (16.3%). Clinical research on AATD treatments includes human and recombinant protein therapies delivered intravenously, by inhalation or subcutaneously, as well as gene- and RNA-based therapies. Additional approaches, such as AAT protein folding correctors and neutrophil elastase inhibitors, are under investigation. Currently, RNA interference therapeutics are the most advanced therapeutic approach, with Phase 3 clinical trials ongoing. The development of novel therapies holds promise to broaden treatment options for patients with AATD, targeting both pulmonary and extrapulmonary manifestations. Not applicable.

title: RRM2 Suppresses Ferroptosis via the MAPK-ERK1/2 Axis to Promote Uterine Leiomyosarcoma Progression.
abstract: 1. Employ bioinformatics and clinical sample analysis to determine the expression level of ribonucleotide reductase subunit M2 (RRM2) in uterine leiomyosarcoma (uLMS) tissues. 2. Explore the impact of RRM2 on the biological behavior of uLMS cells. 3. Investigate the mechanism by which RRM2 contributes to uLMS progression. 1. Bioinformatics analysis of RRM2 expression in uterine leiomyosarcoma (uLMS) using public databases. 2. Collect fresh clinical specimens of uLMS and normal uterine smooth muscle tissues, and culture uLMS cell lines. Detect the relative expression levels of RRM2 by RT-qPCR, Western blot, and immunohistochemistry (IHC). Examine the subcellular localization of RRM2 by immunofluorescence staining. 3. Establish RRM2 knockdown and overexpression uLMS cell lines using small interfering RNA (siRNA) and overexpression plasmids, respectively. Evaluate the effects of RRM2 on the biological behaviors of uLMS cells through CCK-8 assay, EdU incorporation assay, Transwell migration/invasion assay, flow cytometry, and tube formation assay. 4. Identify potential downstream signaling pathways regulated by RRM2 through transcriptome sequencing and bioinformatics analysis, followed by experimental validation. 5. Design rescue experiments to further verify whether RRM2 promotes uLMS progression by regulating the MAPK-ERK1/2 axis to inhibit ferroptosis. 6. Establish stable RRM2 knockdown uLMS cell lines and construct subcutaneous xenograft tumor models in nude mice to evaluate the effects of RRM2 knockdown, ERK inhibitors, and ferroptosis inhibitors on tumor growth in vivo. Detect the expression of Ki67, p-ERK, and GPX4 in tumor tissues by Western blot and IHC. 1. Bioinformatics analysis using the GEPIA database revealed that RRM2 expression was significantly upregulated in uterine sarcoma. 2. RT-qPCR, Western blot, and IHC experiments demonstrated that RRM2 expression was markedly elevated in both uLMS tissues and cell lines compared to normal controls. 3. Cellular functional assays indicated that RRM2 knockdown significantly suppressed cell proliferation, migration, invasion, and angiogenic capabilities while promoting apoptosis, whereas RRM2 overexpression enhanced the malignant phenotype of uLMS cells. 4. KEGG and GSEA analyses of transcriptome sequencing data suggested that RRM2 may promote uLMS progression by inhibiting ferroptosis through the MAPK-ERK1/2 axis, which was further validated by Western blot experiments. 5. Rescue experiments confirmed that RRM2 promotes uLMS progression by regulating the MAPK-ERK1/2 signaling pathway to inhibit ferroptosis. 6. Subcutaneous xenograft experiments in nude mice demonstrated that RRM2 knockdown suppressed tumor growth and combination treatment with ERK inhibitors produced enhanced antitumor effects that were reversible upon administration of ferroptosis inhibitors and both Western blot and IHC analyses confirmed that RRM2 drives malignant progression of uLMS by regulating the MAPK-ERK1/2 signaling pathway to inhibit ferroptosis. This study reveals that RRM2 is significantly upregulated in uLMS, and both in vitro and in vivo experiments further demonstrate that RRM2 drives the malignant progression of uLMS by inhibiting ferroptosis through regulation of the MAPK-ERK1/2 signaling pathway. RRM2 represents a potential candidate diagnostic biomarker for uLMS, providing novel insights for clinical treatment strategies.

title: Transcriptomic Profiling Identifies Hub Transcription Factors Associated with the Protective Effects of Licochalcone A Against HFD-Induced MASLD.
abstract: Metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease (MASLD, formerly NAFLD) lacks approved specific pharmacological treatments and exhibits complex pathogenesis. Licochalcone A (LA), a flavonoid extracted from Glycyrrhiza glabra, possesses anti-inflammatory and lipid-modulating activities, yet its protective effects and transcriptional regulatory mechanisms against MASLD remain poorly defined. We established an HFD-induced MASLD mouse model to assess the in-vivo protective effect of LA. Hepatic RNA-sequencing was performed to profile transcription factor (TF) expression and identify differentially expressed transcription factors (DE-TFs). Functional enrichment and protein-protein interaction (PPI) network analysis were conducted to characterize DE-TFs and screen hub TFs. RT-qPCR was used to validate the expression patterns of identified hub TFs. LA administration attenuated hepatic lipid deposition in HFD-fed MASLD mice. In total, 149 DE-TFs were identified, including 95 DE-TFs from the comparison of HFD versus control mice and 122 DE-TFs from LA-treated mice versus HFD mice, with 68 DE-TFs shared between the two comparisons. Functional enrichment indicated that these DE-TFs were associated with RNA polymerase II-dependent transcription, nuclear components, DNA binding, signal transduction, and metabolic-disease-related pathways. Nine hub TFs (Myc, Fos, Runx1, Mef2c, Spi1, Sox9, E2f1, Cebpa, and Pparg) were screened via PPI analysis. Seven hub TFs were up-regulated, while Cebpa and Pparg were down-regulated in MASLD mice; LA intervention partly reversed this dysregulated expression profile, as further verified by RT-qPCR. LA mitigates the development of HFD-provoked MASLD-associated hepatic lesions and is associated with partially restored transcript levels of aberrantly expressed hub TFs in mice. This work provides transcriptome-level resources for understanding LA-mediated hepatoprotection against HFD-induced MASLD development and highlights candidate TF targets relevant to MASLD research.

title: Physiological and Transcriptome Analysis of Polygonatum cyrtonema Under Continuous Drought Stress.
abstract: Against the backdrop of global warming and the increasingly uneven distribution of water resources, drought has emerged as a critical abiotic stressor limiting the growth and quality formation of medicinal plants. In this study, Polygonatum cyrtonema was subjected to a continuous drought treatment experiment by withholding water for 5, 10, and 20 days, alongside a well-watered control (CK), to preliminarily investigate its physiological responses and transcriptomic alterations under water-deficit conditions. Physiological measurements revealed that prolonged drought stress significantly increased the concentrations of malondialdehyde (MDA) and hydrogen peroxide (H2O2) in leaves, accompanied by elevated in superoxide dismutase (SOD) and peroxidase (POD) activities, as well as increased chlorophyll content. RNA-seq analysis identified a substantial number of differentially expressed genes (DEGs), with 11,835, 12,110, and 11,416 DEGs in the D5, D10, and D20 vs. CK comparisons, respectively, including 6133 shared core DEGs. KEGG enrichment analysis indicated that these DEGs were primarily involved in starch and sucrose metabolism, phenylpropanoid biosynthesis, and plant hormone signal transduction. Weighted gene co-expression network analysis (WGCNA) identified a specific gene module (black module) containing 1681 genes that was highly positively correlated with drought duration (r = 0.95). Protein-protein interaction (PPI) network analysis of this module highlighted several candidate hub genes, including WRKY33 (BMK_Unigene_251623), EDA39 (BMK_Unigene_034545), OHP (BMK_Unigene_221621), and RD20 (BMK_Unigene_149641). Furthermore, genes within the black module were significantly enriched in metabolic pathways such as anthocyanin, phenylpropanoid, and isoflavonoid biosynthesis, as well as phenylalanine, tyrosine, tryptophan, arginine, and proline metabolism. RT-qPCR validation confirmed the expression patterns of these candidate genes, supporting the reliability of the transcriptomic data. Collectively, these findings provide transcriptomic insights into the continuous drought response in P. cyrtonema, and identify candidate genes and pathways for future functional validation and stress-resilience improvement in this species.

title: Machine Learning-Based Screening and Experimental Validation of PIK3C2A as a Candidate Angiogenesis-Related Molecule in Pulmonary Hypertension.
abstract: Pulmonary hypertension (PH) is a progressive cardiopulmonary disease characterized by pulmonary vascular remodeling and dysregulated angiogenesis. However, the angiogenesis-related molecular mechanisms underlying PH remain incompletely understood, and reliable diagnostic biomarkers are still lacking. Therefore, To identify angiogenesis-related key molecules in PH through integrated transcriptomic analyses and experimental validation, we aimed to establish a candidate molecular signature and evaluate the discriminative potential of PIK3C2A. Specifically, GSE15197 was used as the primary bulk-transcriptomic discovery dataset, whereas GSE1909 for cross-species validation, and human pulmonary artery single-cell RNA sequencing data (GSE210248) for cellular characterization. Moreover, Functional enrichment, Weighted Gene Co-expression Network Analysis (WGCNA), immune infiltration analysis, and three machine learning algorithms-logistic regression, random forest (RF), and Least Absolute Shrinkage and Selection Operator (LASSO) were performed to identify model genes. In addition, Single-cell analyses were performed using GSE210248, followed by quantitative real-time polymerase chain reaction (qRT-PCR) validation of candidate-gene expression in monocrotaline (MCT) and Sugen5416 plus hypoxia (SuHx) rat models. As a result, Forty-three angiogenesis-related differentially expressed genes (ARDEGs) were identified and were enriched in terms and pathways related to angiogenesis, vascular development, extracellular matrix organization, and HIF-1 signaling. Four model genes (DCN, DKK1, PIK3C2A, and UNC5B) were identified and showed moderate-to-high discrimination between PH and control samples in GSE15197. Among these genes, PIK3C2A showed its highest expression in endothelial cells, while complementary immune-infiltration and CellChat (version 2.1.1) analyses characterized the broader immune-stromal context of the angiogenesis-related signature. qRT-PCR further confirmed significant downregulation of PIK3C2A in the lungs and pulmonary arteries of MCTand SuHxinduced PH models (p < 0.05). In conclusion, An angiogenesis-related candidate molecular signature comprising DCN, DKK1, PIK3C2A and UNC5B was identified in PH. Among these genes, PIK3C2A showed preferential endothelial expression and was downregulated in both the MCT and SuHx rat PH models, supporting its further evaluation as a candidate molecule associated with PH.

title: Electromagnetic Modulation of the ALS Transcriptome: Toward a Non-Drug Therapeutic Strategy.
abstract: Amyotrophic lateral sclerosis (ALS) is a fatal neurodegenerative disease hallmarked by progressive loss of neuromuscular junctions, cortical and spinal motor neurons (MNs), resulting in muscle paralysis. MNs are particularly vulnerable due to their long axons and high metabolic demands. ALS pathology involves impaired RNA metabolism, protein aggregation, cytoskeletal defects affecting organelle trafficking, and mitochondrial dysfunction, ultimately leading to neurodegeneration. Current treatments only marginally extend survival, calling for alternative therapies. We recently reported beneficial effects of electromagnetic alternating field stimulation (ACMS) on axonal regeneration and organelle motility in ALS. Here, we used iPSC-derived spinal MNs from familial ALS patients with FUS mutations to optimize magnetic field parameters regarding frequency, amplitude and duration. Using compartmentalized neuron cultures, we also tested different magnetic field orientations relative to axons. Following ACMS, we assessed axonal organelle trafficking and the nuclear DNA damage response (DDR) by live-cell imaging. Untreated ALS neurons showed clear defects in both assays. Exposure to magnetic AC sine waves above a threshold amplitude of 7 mT, applied perpendicular to the axonal plane with an optimal low frequency of 25 Hz, led to a sustained boost of mitochondrial and lysosomal motility for over one week and rehabilitation of DDR. These phenotypic improvements correlated with global transcriptomic changes revealed by RNA-sequencing. These phenotypic improvements correlated with global transcriptomic changes revealed by RNA-sequencing. While untreated mutant and wild-type neurons displayed different gene expression profiles, ACMS converged them to a novel, harmonized transcriptional state across all lines. Further analysis of differentially expressed genes (DEGs) yielded a conceptual model in which ACMS activates extracellular matrix (ECM)-mediated cell adhesion and neurotransmitter receptor, ion channel and kinase signaling pathways, ultimately modulating gene transcription and, thereby, motor- and microtubule-associated proteins. This model provides a framework for follow-up studies to experimentally validate the underlying mechanisms and assess the therapeutic potential of ACMS as an alternative biophysical treatment modality for neurodegenerative diseases.

title: Multi-Omics and RNAi Reveal a Role for the Ubiquitin-Proteasome Pathway in Muscle Fiber Development of Common Carp (Cyprinus carpio).
abstract: To investigate the molecular mechanisms of muscle fiber development underlying locomotion differences between two common carp (Cyprinus carpio) strains cultured in a rice-fish symbiosis system, we conducted comparative transcriptomic and proteomic analyses of muscle tissues collected from indolent Congjiang (CJ) and active FFRC No. 2 (FR) strains cultured under identical paddy field conditions. RNA-seq revealed 3708 differentially expressed genes (DEGs), and proteomic analysis identified 108 differentially expressed proteins (DEPs). Functional enrichment and protein-protein interaction (PPI) network analyses highlighted key genes (psma3, ppargc1a, ube3a) and proteins (Myh, Ckmt2b, Suclg2) associated with proteasome activity, adipocytokine signaling, and ubiquitin-mediated protein degradation. Quantitative PCR (RT-qPCR) analysis of ubiquitin-proteasome pathway-related genes confirmed significantly higher expression levels in the muscle tissue of CJ compared with FR. After a 21-day interference experiment, ube3a knockdown increased average muscle fiber area and diameter and reduced muscle fiber density in juvenile CJ, indicating that ube3a knockdown might promote muscle development in common carp. Subsequent swimming performance measurements can be conducted to further explore the impact of ube3a on fish locomotion. These results provide molecular insights into fish locomotion capacity related to behavioral adaptation in agroecological systems.

title: STAT3 Signaling Contributes to Chemokine Production in E2-Induced Dermal Inflammation.
abstract: Scleroderma (SSc) is characterized by dermal inflammation and fibrosis. Patients with SSc have elevated circulating levels of estradiol (E2) that contribute to dermal fibrosis. Using bulk RNA sequencing (RNA-seq), we investigated inflammatory pathways in E2 or ethanol (ETOH, vehicle)-treated human skin tissue for 48 h to identify differentially expressed genes (DEGs) and enriched pathways. Among the 90 DEGs responsive to E2 treatment, many were associated with enriched inflammatory pathways. Likewise, cytokine and chemokine activities were among the most significantly enriched molecular function terms. qPCR and protein analyses demonstrated increased cytokine and chemokine expression in primary dermal fibroblasts. CIBERSORTx deconvolution using a skin single-cell reference suggested an activated fibroblast transcriptional signature in E2-treated human skin tissue. In this tissue, E2-induced IL-6 and CXCL8 transcript levels were positively correlated. Pharmacologic STAT3 inhibition reduced E2-induced CXCL2, CXCL3, CXCL8, and CCL20 transcript levels in human skin tissue. In SSc dermal fibroblasts, anastrozole treatment significantly decreased CXCL3 and CXCL8 transcript levels. Together, these data suggest that E2 contributes, in part, to increased CXCL2, CXCL3, CXCL8, and CCL20 transcripts and that IL-6/STAT3 signaling may be important in this dermal inflammatory response.

title: Senescence-Related Transcriptomic Analysis and Functional Characterization of ANGPTL4 in Lung Adenocarcinoma.
abstract: Background: Cellular senescence and the senescence-associated secretory phenotype (SASP) can alter communication between tumor cells and the surrounding microenvironment, but the extracellular mediators involved in this process remain poorly defined in lung adenocarcinoma (LUAD). Methods: Bulk transcriptomic analysis was used to characterize senescence-related transcriptional alterations and construct a prognostic signature. ANGPTL4 expression was evaluated in public datasets and clinical samples. Single-cell RNA-sequencing analysis was then performed to map senescence-associated gene-set scores across LUAD cell populations and to examine the cell-cell communication. ANGPTL4 depletion and overexpression were used to assess its effects on LUAD-cell proliferation, migration, and SA-β-gal positivity, while a subcutaneous xenograft model was used to examine tumor growth in vivo. Conditioned-medium and indirect co-culture experiments were performed to assess the effects of ANGPTL4-overexpressing LUAD cells on THP-1-derived macrophage inflammatory responses, and MCC950 was used to evaluate the contribution of NLRP3-associated signaling. Results: Senescence-related transcriptional alterations in LUAD were enriched in inflammatory and immune-related pathways. ANGPTL4 was included in a five-gene prognostic model and selected for functional investigation because it encodes a secreted protein. We found that ANGPTL4 protein levels were increased in LUAD tissues. Single-cell analysis showed relatively high senescence-associated gene-set scores in macrophage-enriched populations, together with stronger cell-cell communication in the higher-score group. ANGPTL4 depletion reduced LUAD-cell migration and SA-β-gal positivity, while its overexpression had the opposite effects and resulted in larger xenograft tumors. Conditioned medium and indirect co-culture experiments showed that ANGPTL4-overexpressing LUAD cells induced inflammatory changes in THP-1-derived macrophages, accompanied by increased NLRP3-associated markers and IL-1β secretion. These changes were partly attenuated by MCC950. Conclusions: These findings suggest that ANGPTL4 is associated with tumor cell-macrophage crosstalk in LUAD and may correlate with senescence-related transcriptional signatures, while the specific biological role of ANGPTL4 remains to be further characterized.

title: Single-Cell Transcriptomic and Regulatory Network Analyses Identify a Putative HNF4A-OXR1 Association Linked to Podocyte Mitochondrial Dysfunction in Diabetic Kidney Disease.
abstract: Podocyte injury is a central pathological event in diabetic kidney disease (DKD), but the mitochondrial regulatory mechanisms underlying podocyte dysfunction remain incompletely defined. We integrated single-nucleus RNA-seq data from human renal biopsies in GSE195460 with podocyte-specific differential expression, functional enrichment, mitochondrial gene annotation, co-expression network analysis, machine learning feature selection, pseudotime analysis, in silico knockout, transcription factor enrichment, motif analysis, and molecular docking; findings were externally evaluated in GSE209781. Podocytes showed prominent disease-associated transcriptomic perturbation, with 677 exploratory cell-level differentially expressed genes and enrichment of cytoskeletal, adhesion, developmental, oxidative phosphorylation, and metabolic pathways. Thirty-one mitochondrial-related differentially expressed genes were identified, and OXR1 was prioritized as a candidate regulatory hub based on consistent downregulation, network centrality, machine learning selection, and external validation. HNF4A was predicted as an upstream regulator linked to OXR1 and other mitochondrial targets. In silico OXR1 perturbation increased the predicted injured-state probability from 15% to 82%, while promoter motif analysis provided additional computational support for a putative HNF4A-OXR1 regulatory relationship. These findings highlight OXR1 as a candidate associated with podocyte mitochondrial dysfunction in DKD and suggest a putative HNF4A-OXR1 regulatory relationship.

title: Integrated Transcriptomic Analysis Identifies a Ferroptosis-Related Gene Signature Underlying Macrophage Heterogeneity and Immune Dysregulation in Rheumatoid Arthritis Synovium.
abstract: Ferroptosis contributes to rheumatoid arthritis (RA), but the key regulators and their cell-specific functions in the synovial microenvironment remain incompletely understood. This study aimed to identify robust ferroptosis-associated biomarkers and define their cellular context through an integrated transcriptomic framework. Bulk synovial transcriptomic datasets were integrated using differential expression, weighted gene co-expression network analysis, and a curated ferroptosis gene set. Candidate genes were prioritized using three feature-selection algorithms and validated across twelve models. Immune infiltration, single-cell RNA sequencing, pseudotime, CellChat, and virtual gene perturbation analyses characterized their cellular and functional context. Six ferroptosis-related genes (AIM2, HCP5, CAPG, ALOX5, TYMS, and RUNX3) formed a diagnostic signature discriminating RA from healthy synovium (mean leakage-free test AUC 0.977 across five training-only re-derivations; 0.9375 in the primary split), with consistent leave-one-dataset-out and osteoarthritis-control validation. These genes linked to adaptive immune and ferroptosis-associated transcriptional programs. Single-cell analysis localized this transcriptional score to macrophages, where ferroptosis-signature-high macrophages occupied a central communication-network position and showed collagen-pathway enrichment; because RA and healthy samples were not fully independent of dataset origin, this finding is hypothesis-generating. Pseudotime analysis suggested progressive induction of these genes toward an inflammatory NF-κB/TNF/IL-17 terminal state, and virtual perturbation suggested convergence on mitochondrial oxidative phosphorylation networks that persisted after removing sex-chromosome genes, though residual sex-associated effects cannot be fully excluded. This study identifies a biologically interpretable ferroptosis-related gene signature and suggests ferroptosis-associated macrophage reprogramming may contribute to immune dysregulation in RA synovium. The single-cell findings are hypothesis-generating given the cohort design, while the diagnostic signature was supported by leakage-free, cross-cohort, and disease-specificity analyses, providing candidate biomarkers and therapeutic targets for RA.

title: The Cholecystokinin-B Receptor as a Candidate Diagnostic Biomarker and Translational Target for Precision Oncology in Pancreatic Cancer.
abstract: Background/Objectives: Identification of cell-surface receptors on cancer tissues that are absent in the corresponding normal tissue provide an opportunity for target-specific diagnostics and drug delivery. The cholecystokinin-B receptor (CCKBR) was initially overlooked as a high-priority biomarker for pancreatic cancer (PDAC) because comparisons were made between cancer and "normal adjacent tissue" from The Cancer Genome Atlas (TCGA). Since PDAC is highly invasive and significantly alters the tumor microenvironment, we now know the adjacent tissue is not normal in PDAC. Methods: A multi-cohort transcriptomic analysis was conducted to evaluate the true expression landscape of CCKBR in human pancreatic tissue. Bulk RNA-sequencing data were harmonized from the Genotype-Tissue Expression (GTEx) repository (N = 328) with true normal pancreas samples and TCGA Pancreatic Adenocarcinoma cohort (N = 178) primary tumors. Confirmation of CCKBR protein expression was performed using a human tissue array. The significance of a single-nucleotide polymorphism (SNP, rs1800843) that results in CCKBR mis-splicing was characterized. A biodegradable fluorescent polyplex nanoparticle (NP) was developed to selectively target the CCKBR and was tested using p48-Cre/LSL-KrasG12D (KC) mice. Results: CCKBR transcripts exhibited a profound, binary-like upregulation in malignant tissue compared to normal tissue, achieving statistical significance (p = 10-60). The germline SNP of the CCKBR (rs1800843) was identified in ~40% of patients with confirmed PDAC. Immunoreactivity for the CCKBR protein was absent in normal human pancreas but increased in precancerous PanIN lesions and cancer. A fluorescent labeled CCKBR-targeted NP revealed uptake in the pancreas of KC mice and localized to the PanIN lesions. Conclusions: These data provide new insights into CCKBR, supporting its potential as a diagnostic biomarker and a therapeutic target in precision pancreatic oncology.

title: TSPO and LRBA Expression Is Associated with Acute Renal Allograft Rejection: An Integrative Transcriptomic Analysis.
abstract: Acute renal transplant rejection causes allograft injury and affects long-term graft survival. Mitophagy helps maintain mitochondrial homeostasis and regulate immune function, but its relationship with acute rejection remains unclear. We integrated public renal allograft transcriptomic datasets using differential expression analysis, weighted gene co-expression network analysis, and machine learning. We performed external cohort validation, survival analysis, immune deconvolution, single-cell RNA sequencing analysis, virtual knockout analysis, and quantitative PCR in mouse renal allografts. Among 32 shared mitophagy-associated genes which we identified, TSPO was consistently upregulated and LRBA was downregulated across independent biopsy cohorts. An exploratory TSPO/LRBA two-gene model showed modest discrimination between rejection and non-rejection samples. Higher model scores were associated with poorer graft survival. An exploratory analysis of the model was then performed in peripheral blood. Functional and single-cell analyses linked these genes to monocyte/macrophage populations, antigen presentation, T-cell signaling, and inflammatory pathways. Virtual knockout analysis predicted changes in antigen presentation, phagocytosis, and allograft rejection pathways. Quantitative PCR confirmed increased TSPO and decreased LRBA expression in mouse renal allografts with acute rejection. Together, these findings identify TSPO and LRBA as new candidate mitophagy-associated biomarkers linked to monocytes/macrophages and support further investigation of their associations with acute renal transplant rejection.

title: Low MATR3 Expression Is Associated with Poor Prognosis in Endometrial Carcinoma: An Integrated Immunohistochemical and Transcriptomic Analysis.
abstract: Endometrial carcinoma (EC) is the most common malignancy of the female genital tract, yet reliable prognostic biomarkers remain limited. Matrin-3 (MATR3), a nuclear matrix protein involved in genome stability and RNA processing, has been implicated in various cancers, but its role in EC has not been described. Here, we performed an integrated analysis combining immunohistochemical evaluation of MATR3 protein expression in a retrospective institutional cohort of 112 patients with EC and in silico analysis of MATR3 mRNA expression in 172 TCGA cases. Immunohistochemical analysis revealed nuclear MATR3 expression in both EC and normal endometrial tissues, with significantly lower protein levels in EC compared to control tissues (p < 0.0001). MATR3 mRNA was significantly reduced in EC tumour tissues compared to adjacent normal tissues (p < 0.0001). Low MATR3 protein expression was associated with shorter OS after adjustment for age, histological grade, pT, pN and pM in an LVSI-stratified Cox model (HR = 2.296; 95% CI: 1.284-4.104; p = 0.0050). Low MATR3 mRNA expression was associated with improved overall survival in TCGA (median OS = 110.1 months; HR = 2.174; 95% CI: 1.066-4.43; p = 0.0303). Co-expression analysis identified BCLAF1 and TOP2B as key positive correlates, while TRAPPC5 and FASTK showed the strongest negative correlations.
