Genes positively correlated with MATR3 mRNA expression were enriched for nuclear transcription and RNA-processing annotations, whereas negatively correlated genes were enriched for mitochondrial processes. These associations do not establish a mechanistic link between MATR3 and pathway activity. Our findings support further investigation of MATR3 as a candidate prognostic marker in EC, with independent validation and functional studies required.

title: Spatial Transcriptomics in Chronic Rhinosinusitis: Deciphering Tissue Architecture, Immune Niches, and Precision Therapeutics.
abstract: Chronic rhinosinusitis (CRS) is a heterogeneous inflammatory disorder in which epithelial injury, immune activation, and stromal remodelling are organised into local tissue niches. Bulk and single-cell RNA sequencing have defined important cell states, but dissociation removes the anatomical relationships needed to determine where those states coexist. Spatial transcriptomics (ST) addresses this gap by mapping RNA, and in some platforms, protein, onto intact sinonasal tissue. This review provides an evidence-graded synthesis organised around a single translational chain: spatial niche to molecular signature to plausible biological mechanism to CRS phenotype/endotype to clinical implication to therapeutic relevance to validation status. Direct CRS ST evidence is separated from single-cell RNA sequencing support, computational prediction, protein or in situ evidence, experimental perturbation, clinical validation, and extrapolation from other inflammatory diseases. Current CRS studies support spatial compartmentalisation of eosinophil-rich epithelial lesions, ALOX15-positive macrophage programmes, GZMK-positive CD8 T-cell-fibroblast neighbourhoods, and treatment-associated epithelial and stromal changes. However, most ligand-receptor calls remain predictive, and spatial association alone does not establish functional causality. ST is therefore best viewed as a discovery and mechanistic-prioritisation technology whose clinical promises-biomarker selection, biologic matching, and response monitoring-require independent cohorts, locked assays, patient-level reproducibility, and prospective outcome studies. We compare study designs and platforms, examine statistical issues including spatial autocorrelation and pseudoreplication, and propose a cautious translational framework in which orthogonal and clinical validation convert spatial observations into actionable evidence.

title: A Lymphoid-Enriched Spatial Immune Niche Defines an Immunotherapy-Responsive State in Hepatocellular Carcinoma.
abstract: Atezolizumab plus bevacizumab is a first-line therapy for advanced hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC), yet only a subset of patients achieve durable benefit. The spatial organization of the tumour microenvironment (TME) and its relationship to immunotherapy response remain incompletely understood. We integrated single-cell transcriptomics, spatial transcriptomics, spatial proteomics, and bulk RNA-sequencing cohorts to characterize spatially organized immune ecosystems associated with immunotherapy response in HCC. Single-cell RNA sequencing from 100 HCC samples was used to construct a cellular reference, which was integrated with spatial transcriptomics from 12 sections to identify nine consensus spatial niches. Niche 9 represented a lymphoid-enriched immune state characterized by B cells, plasma cells, natural killer cells, T-cell subsets, macrophages, and tertiary lymphoid structure-associated transcriptional features. Independent validation in a pretreatment, response-annotated Visium cohort showed enrichment of Niche 9-associated transcriptional activity in immunotherapy responders, while spatially co-registered 51-plex CODEX profiling provided orthogonal protein-level support for its lymphoid and immune-enriched phenotype. Multi-omics characterization further revealed coordinated immune-cell localization, ligand-receptor-associated patterns, and distinct metabolic programmes, with MEI1-positive plasma cells displaying enhanced secretory and stress-adaptation states. A nine-gene transcriptional signature derived from Niche 9 was associated with atezolizumab-plus-bevacizumab response, enhanced lymphoid immune features, lower Tumour Immune Dysfunction and Exclusion scores, and favourable clinical outcomes in independent cohorts. These multi-cohort and multi-omics analyses define a spatially derived lymphoid-enriched immune programme and link its molecular features to immunotherapy sensitivity in HCC.

title: Transcriptomic Alterations in Peripheral Blood of Patients with Metabolic Syndrome.
abstract: Metabolic syndrome (MetS) is a complex cardiometabolic disorder characterized by interconnected abnormalities in glucose and lipid metabolism, adiposity, and vascular regulation. Transcriptomic profiling may provide insight into molecular alterations associated with MetS. This study aimed to identify peripheral blood gene expression changes in MetS using RNA sequencing and to evaluate selected candidate genes by RT-qPCR in an independent cohort. RNA sequencing was performed in 15 patients with MetS and 10 healthy controls; after exclusion of three MetS samples based on PCA, differential expression analysis included 12 patients with MetS and 10 controls. Six candidate genes (FKBP1B, PLIN2, ARVCF, NAA40, ALOX15B, and MUSTN1) were subsequently evaluated by RT-qPCR in an independent cohort of 146 patients with MetS and 116 controls. Relative expression changes were calculated using the 2^-ΔΔCt method, and multiple testing was controlled using the Benjamini-Hochberg false discovery rate (FDR) procedure. Among 19,668 protein-coding genes, 730 showed nominal differential expression (p < 0.05), whereas only FKBP1B and EVA1C remained significant after FDR correction. In the RT-qPCR cohort, FKBP1B, ARVCF, and NAA40 showed significantly higher expression in MetS, corresponding to 6.33-, 1.87-, and 2.34-fold increases, respectively; all remained significant after FDR correction. No significant differences were observed for PLIN2, ALOX15B, or MUSTN1. Exploratory analyses identified no robust associations between candidate-gene expression and metabolic or cardiovascular clinical parameters after multiple-testing correction. FKBP1B remained significant after transcriptome-wide FDR correction and showed concordant upregulation in the independent RT-qPCR cohort, while the nominal RNA-seq candidates ARVCF and NAA40 also showed significantly increased expression by RT-qPCR. These findings identify transcriptional alterations associated with MetS and warrant further validation in independent cohorts and functional studies.

title: Integrative Single-Cell and Radiomics Analyses Identify N-Acetylneuraminate Synthase (NANS)-High Signature Associated with Adverse Prognosis and Immune Remodeling in Glioblastoma.
abstract: Glioblastoma (GBM) is characterized by marked heterogeneity and an immunosuppressive microenvironment. N-acetylneuraminate synthase (NANS) contributes to tumor-associated metabolic regulation, but its relationship with GBM and its immune profile remains unclear. This study aimed to characterize the prognostic and immune relevance of NANS and develop an MRI radiomics model for noninvasive prediction of NANS-high GBM. Prognostic genes were screened across TCGA-GBM and two CGGA cohorts. Bulk transcriptomic and single-cell RNA sequencing analyses were used to evaluate NANS expression, patient survival association, and cellular localization. NANS-high bone marrow-derived macrophages (BMDMs) were characterized using functional enrichment and CellChat analyses. A NANS-high BMDM signature was validated in TCGA-GBM for immune infiltration and ligand-receptor axis activity. Drug sensitivity and CMap analyses were performed. MRI radiomics features were extracted from preprocessed T1 contrast-enhanced and FLAIR images, and an elastic net logistic regression model was constructed to predict NANS-high BMDM signature status. NANS was identified as a prognostic macrophage-associated biomarker in GBM and was enriched in BMDMs. NANS-high BMDMs showed enrichment of mTORC1 signaling, oxidative phosphorylation, unfolded protein response, glycolysis, hypoxia, and protein secretion programs. Cell-cell communication analysis revealed enhanced outgoing signaling toward malignant tumor states and T-cell subsets, with LGALS9-centered interactions representing the dominant differential communication program. In TCGA-GBM, the NANS-high BMDM signature correlated with increased macrophage infiltration, broad immune infiltration, and elevated LGALS9 and PLAU axis scores. Drug sensitivity analyses suggested potential vulnerabilities involving PI3K/mTOR and MAPK/ERK pathways. The radiomics model selected six MRI features and distinguished NANS-high from NANS-low tumors with an AUC of 0.795 (95% CI, 0.652-0.939); bootstrap validation showed a mean AUC of 0.793 (95% CI, 0.637-0.922). NANS-high BMDMs define a prognostically adverse and potentially targetable macrophage-associated phenotype in GBM. MRI radiomics may noninvasively predict this NANS-high BMDM state, supporting imaging-based risk stratification and therapeutic selection.
